descs.en: He forgot to thank her. She sat on his desk until he looked up. Ten minutes, every night at nine, until Lima needed her more.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Inspector Song Wei Long is collecting an extradited fraudster at the airport when the paperwork collapses, in a language nobody at the custody desk speaks. A Canadian consular officer in a soaked coat fixes it in three languages in eleven minutes. He says Correct, and forgets to thank her. She leaves a card under his windscreen wiper to tell him so.

A week later she’s sitting on his desk at nine at night, on top of his files, telling him the world can wait ten minutes. It does. Then a body comes out of the harbour, he fires his gun in a stairwell, and Isla is offered the posting she has wanted for years: three years in Lima, thirteen hours away.

The man who has never asked anyone for anything has to learn to say go, and mean it. And then, when the ground moves, to get on a plane.

She sits on his desk · Stoic hero · Long distance · Complete in four volumes, plus ten side stories

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Wei Long has been at the edge of every Lin book: the inspector at the door, the one who already knows. I wanted to know who he went home to. The answer was nobody, and then a woman who sat on his desk.

This isn’t a slow burn. The ice goes in a week. What’s hard is everything after: a shooting he has to answer for, a posting on the other side of the world, an earthquake, and a man learning to ask the woman he loves what she wants.

The police work and the consular work are as real as I could make them. The ten minutes are true.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers.

Dry, funny and warm, with real police cases shown plainly. It includes:

• Love scenes on the page throughout, from the first week

• A woman strangled and found in the harbour, and her post-mortem

• A stalker

• A police shooting, on the page, and the review that follows

• A death in police custody abroad

• A major earthquake: the dead, the missing, an aftershock

• Fear and grief during a long silence

chapters.title: Three Languages in a Wet Terminal
chapters.desc: An extradited fraudster arrives on the wrong form, in a language nobody at the custody desk speaks, and a consular officer in a soaked coat fixes it in eleven minutes in English, French and Chinese. Inspector Song watches her the whole time and forgets to thank her. Cold, clipped, funny; no heat yet but the look.
chapters.epigraph: “You forgot thank you.”

chapters.title: She Calls the Station
chapters.desc: She rings the station to check the prisoner arrived. He answers his own desk phone, which nobody in the squad room has ever seen. She asks him to dinner; he writes Friday on his hand.
chapters.epigraph: “Do you always sound like a glacier?”

chapters.title: The Inspector Who Forgot Dinner
chapters.desc: He forgets: a stabbing at the fish market keeps him till ten. At eleven she walks into the squad room with two boxes of noodles, sits on his desk on top of his files and kisses him first. A first kiss that is hers entirely; mouths, his hands not knowing where to go, six detectives pretending to read.
chapters.epigraph: “The world can wait ten minutes”

chapters.title: A Second Case, a Second Language
chapters.desc: He asks for her by name on a case with a French-speaking witness, a frightened au pair who saw a beating. In Stairwell B afterwards he tells her he’s going to kiss her, and does, against the rail, deep and unhurried. He admits he’s read her consular file.
chapters.epigraph: “Isla. I’m going to kiss you now.”

chapters.title: Ten Minutes on His Desk
chapters.desc: It becomes a rule. Nine o’clock, she sits on his desk, the world waits ten minutes, blinds down. The squad starts timing it. Kisses grow longer and hungrier: her fingers in his collar, his hands on her thighs over her skirt, both stopping at the ten-minute mark because he’s literal.
chapters.epigraph: “Fortunately, I like you too.”

chapters.title: Twelve More Pages of Testimony
chapters.desc: He has to sign twelve pages she translated and can’t get past the first because she’s kissing his neck. She takes the pen out of his hand and takes him home. First night, fully on the page: she undresses him, tells him exactly what she wants, and for once he says nothing at all.
chapters.epigraph: “I have twelve more pages of testimony to sign.”

chapters.title: The Inspector Smiles, Allegedly
chapters.desc: Three officers claim to have seen him smile at a text during a briefing. Nobody can prove it; he denies everything. A pickpocket ring at the cruise terminal; a quick, greedy kiss in the car park because she can’t wait for nine.
chapters.epigraph: “Because I wanted to kiss you now.”

chapters.title: The First Dinner He Remembers
chapters.desc: He arrives early with flowers he doesn’t know the name of. Over dinner he tells her one true thing: his grandfather, Old Song, walked the Walled City beat for thirty years and he did his homework at the station desk. At his flat the scanner on the bedside table is ignored. Explicit, slower than the first: he takes his time and narrates nothing.
chapters.epigraph: “He used to say that if you walked the same streets long enough, people stopped seeing the uniform.”

chapters.title: Her Brother Storms the Station
chapters.desc: Ren Hao finds out from someone else’s photo and comes to the front desk at volume. Wei Long takes him into an interview room and reads him his rights as a joke nobody laughs at. Isla takes both their phones away and makes them shake hands.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going anywhere because someone is loud.”

chapters.title: Headphones Over the Scanner
chapters.desc: Her one rule at his place: no police radio in bed. He breaks it once, goes out at three for a missing child on the harbour front, and comes back at six with the child found. She takes his boots off. Dawn love scene, slow, explicit, his head on her stomach afterwards.
chapters.epigraph: “But when you come back you take your boots off at the door, you put the radio away, and you come to bed.”

chapters.title: A Video Call With Two Professors
chapters.desc: Her parents in Vancouver, both academics, interview him on video like a dissertation committee. He prepared a written statement. After the call she climbs into his lap; heat, kissing, stopping only because her laptop is still on.
chapters.epigraph: “I would like her to keep choosing me.”

chapters.title: The Man Who Trained Him
chapters.desc: Retired Superintendent Pun, the closest thing he has to a father, wants to meet the woman who sits on his desk, and interrogates her over tea. She interrogates him back and wins.
chapters.epigraph: “Somebody has to know what’s happening.”

chapters.title: The House Next Door Gets Quiet
chapters.desc: Eliana Lin moves into the old Song house next door to her father’s, the house Wei Long left to Yu Chen in summer 2024. Wei Long goes round to sign the last papers and finds he has no home of his own, only a flat he sleeps in. Isla gives him a key to hers, labelled HOME, PROVISIONAL.
chapters.epigraph: “I live here now.”

chapters.title: Growing Up Beside the Walled City
chapters.desc: At two in the morning he tells her what it was to grow up beside the Walled City as a policeman’s grandson, never allowed through the Lins’ red door, and to take on an eight-year-old cousin at fifteen. She kisses the scar on his hand she never asked about.
chapters.epigraph: “He was there. And I was there.”

chapters.title: The Neighbour Asks for Nothing
chapters.desc: Visiting Yu Chen, he’s stopped at the garden wall by Lin Jian, who asks him for nothing, which is worse than asking. Both men know Wei Long knows his daughter is the Eraser, and that the man who knifed Elara is in Wei Long’s cells. Isla, waiting in the car, reads his face.
chapters.epigraph: “That’s worse, isn’t it?”

chapters.title: The Case That Kept Him Away
chapters.desc: A week in a surveillance flat watching a smuggler. She sends him a photograph every night of what he’s missing, none of them of food. Home at dawn on Sunday he doesn’t take his coat off: explicit, fast, against her front door, then slow in bed.
chapters.epigraph: “I promise I’ll come home to you.”

chapters.title: A Body in the Harbour
chapters.desc: A woman is pulled out of the water off the ferry pier: Koon Fan-ling, 26, a visa clerk at Isla’s consulate, strangled and weighted. Isla had lunch with her on Tuesdays. Dark: the post-mortem is shown plainly; Wei Long takes the case and is told he can’t, because of Isla.
chapters.epigraph: “Tomorrow. Don’t be late this time.”

chapters.title: She Is a Witness
chapters.desc: He has to interview her properly, on tape, across a table in Interview Three, and can’t touch her for an hour. She lies to protect a colleague who sold visas, and he catches it. After the tape stops: a furious kiss in the corridor, her back to the wall, teeth.
chapters.epigraph: “She was a person.”

chapters.title: He Breaks Protocol Once
chapters.desc: Someone follows her home three nights running. He stays in her flat with his weapon on the coffee table, against orders. On the third night she won’t let him stay on the sofa. On the fourth morning he reports himself.
chapters.epigraph: “Let me look after you, for once.”

chapters.title: The Arrest
chapters.desc: He finds Yiu in a car-park stairwell with a knife at a second clerk’s throat and shoots him twice. Shown, not softened: the sound, the smell, the man dying on the concrete steps. A long night afterwards; he’s silent for forty minutes, then says it twice.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d do it again.”

chapters.title: A Posting to Lima
chapters.desc: Cleared by the review, he’s given a commendation he doesn’t want. The ministry offers Isla the posting she asked for two years ago: three years in Lima, deputy head of consular. She doesn’t tell him for four days. He finds the letter; she kisses him before he can speak.
chapters.epigraph: “She kissed me before I could speak.”

chapters.title: He Says Go
chapters.desc: The start is moved up to the first week of July and she tells him after six hours, not four days. He says he’s unhappy, out loud, then says go, and means it. The first “I love you” is hers, in passing; his comes straight after. He books his leave and tells no one.
chapters.epigraph: “I love you, Isla”

chapters.title: The Airport, the Wrong Way Round
chapters.desc: The terminal where they met, raining again. He can’t go through security without a ticket, so he sits on a dead check-in counter at aisle forty until she laughs; she kisses him through the security barrier.
chapters.epigraph: “Come home when you’re ready.”

chapters.title: Thirteen Hours
chapters.desc: Thirteen hours apart. His night shift is her morning coffee. She runs her first death-in-custody case abroad. Language cards arrive in his post, one a week; calls get explicit and he hangs up blushing in a stairwell.
chapters.epigraph: “No tengo que hacerlo todo solo.”

chapters.title: The Ground Moves
chapters.desc: A major earthquake off the coast. Phones go down across Lima. He watches the news for twelve hours. Dark: collapsed blocks, the count rising, no word.
chapters.epigraph: “I love you. I’m waiting.”

chapters.title: She Calls From the Embassy’s Shelter
chapters.desc: Two minutes on a satellite phone from the embassy’s shelter. “I’m fine.” He hears the sirens. Four hundred of her citizens are unaccounted for. “I’m coming.” “You can’t.” “Watch me.”
chapters.epigraph: “Watch me.”

chapters.title: He Takes Leave for the First Time in Six Years
chapters.desc: He takes leave for the first time in six years. His sergeant takes the cases without being asked. Ren Hao books the only seat left and pays for it, loudly; he’s on a break from Song-Zhu and badly needs something to fix.
chapters.epigraph: “Six years is a long time, Song. Don’t make it seven.”

chapters.title: He Flies to Her
chapters.desc: His warrant card means nothing at the checkpoint. He finds her asleep on a desk on the ninth floor, a list under her cheek, slides it out without reading it, and waits. She wakes and kisses him before she’s sure he’s real. Then he carries water up nine flights for nine hours.
chapters.epigraph: “I didn’t come to take you home.”

chapters.title: The Glacier in a Foreign City
chapters.desc: He can’t read the signs; she translates everything and reconciles a whole country’s missing against hospital lists. She finds the last name alive: a student in a field hospital, written down the way her surname sounded. A borrowed room with a cracked wall, an aftershock mid-way, and neither stops.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m proud of you.”

chapters.title: He Asks Her What She Wants
chapters.desc: On the cliff path at dusk he asks her what she wants. Nobody has asked her in years and she doesn’t know. He waits. She answers with her mouth on the sea wall, then says she’ll keep the posting for now. On Friday she drives him to the airport.
chapters.epigraph: “What do you want, Isla?”

chapters.title: She Asks for a Transfer Home
chapters.desc: She asks the ministry for a posting home: for herself, not for him. Her head of section, Ruth Ferreira, asks if it’s a man. Wei Long is back in Lima for his last eleven days of leave, and she tells him only when it’s sent, on a bench above the park.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to do anything to keep me.”

chapters.title: The Ministry Says No
chapters.desc: The ministry says no to the deputy job and yes to an emergencies desk at the consulate: a step down on paper. She takes it because she wants the work. He meets her at arrivals with ranunculus, asked for by name; she jumps. His fridge list is still up.
chapters.epigraph: “It was still true.”

chapters.title: She Doesn’t Hate It
chapters.desc: She runs consular emergencies for the whole city, and the station learns her direct line. Nine o’clock, his desk, ten minutes, again. They sign a lease on a bigger flat together, with boxes for furniture: explicit. He takes Qu Wenjun’s one line to Camphor Hill.
chapters.epigraph: “I forgot I was allowed to like the work.”

chapters.title: The Same Interview Room
chapters.desc: Inspector and consular officer, one case, opposite sides of the same table: a citizen of hers accused of manslaughter in a case of his. She won’t tell him what her citizen said. Afterwards, in his car, both of them right, a hard kiss.
chapters.epigraph: “I know where your side is. I sat opposite it today.”

chapters.title: Her Brother Approves, Finally
chapters.desc: Ren Hao approves, finally, in an eleven-minute toast nobody asked for at a dinner nobody wanted. Wei Long holds her hand under the table the whole time. Ren Hao catches them in the corridor and leaves loudly.
chapters.epigraph: “I want the people who love you to know I love you properly.”

chapters.title: Back to the Terminal
chapters.desc: The airport where they met. He proposes by the custody desk at arrivals with a prepared written statement. She says yes into his collar.
chapters.epigraph: “I have loved you in every place between this desk and here, and here is this desk.”

chapters.title: She Corrects His Proposal
chapters.desc: She corrects his proposal in three languages, at home, in bed. Engaged, the first night: explicit, slow, playful; he writes it again on a card, correctly.
chapters.epigraph: “One letter is the difference between a fact and a wish.”

chapters.title: The Forms
chapters.desc: The most romantic paperwork either of them has ever filled in: a notice of marriage, two nationalities, one registry. He reads the declaration three times; she helps the old couple on the bench. A kiss at window four.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s different because we did something about it.”

chapters.title: He Dances, Badly
chapters.desc: At the engagement party everyone films him dancing, and nobody posts it, because she asked. Superintendent Pun and Ren Hao arm in arm. Yu Chen and Eliana leave early for his six o’clock shift. Home, her shoes in his hand: explicit.
chapters.epigraph: “I danced with my fiancée. That’s all.”

chapters.title: Ten Minutes
chapters.desc: Epilogue. Fifty weeks married (registry, Sat 25 Mar 2028). Four years and two days after the terminal, she sits on his desk at nine. He’s already looking. The world waits ten minutes; Hau and Choy bet coins on the windowsill.
chapters.epigraph: “You still look up.”

chapters.title: He Announces the Back Hug
chapters.desc: A drama she makes him watch, a line in his notebook, and a week of planning. Then he tells her he’s going to hug her from behind, which ruins it. She turns round inside it and kisses him against the stove.
chapters.epigraph: “She prefers to know. Sometimes she needs not to.”

chapters.title: Small Talk for Seven Detectives
chapters.desc: Superintendent Chiang asks the consulate for a session on rapport with frightened witnesses. Isla runs small talk for six detectives and a station sergeant in Interview Two. It goes badly for everyone; his score is last.
chapters.epigraph: “I only need to be good at talking to you.”

chapters.title: The Laugh Nobody Recorded
chapters.desc: Sham swears the inspector laughed. Nobody can prove it. Then a pigeon story at home and Isla has six seconds on her phone.
chapters.epigraph: “You sounded happy.”

chapters.title: Arm Wrestling for Her Honour
chapters.desc: Her brother challenges him to arm wrestling across a noodle-shop table, best of five. He wins three, then loses two on purpose; she knows, and tells him in bed.
chapters.epigraph: “They’re yours.”

chapters.title: Herbal Tea Replaces Coffee
chapters.desc: A slow conspiracy by a woman who thinks he drinks too much coffee: thirteen weeks of roasted barley in his grandfather’s green tin. He’s known since he descaled the machine in December.
chapters.epigraph: “You were making me tea.”

chapters.title: The Book on the Ten Minutes
chapters.desc: The squad’s betting book on Isla’s ten minutes, its whole life: Sham’s first sheet, confiscated; Hau running it from the front desk; Tak caught cheating; the entries for Lantern Lane and Lima; Liu winning on the proposal; and why the inspector keeps the first sheet and the last, blank one.
chapters.epigraph: “That you were there.”

chapters.title: Language Cards in His Pockets
chapters.desc: After Lima she goes on writing him language cards, and leaves them in every jacket he owns. Twelve words, used at the worst moments. The twelfth is in his shirt pocket: rendirse. Explicit.
chapters.epigraph: “Not because you’ve lost. Because you trust whoever is holding you.”

chapters.title: The Stakeout Picnic
chapters.desc: She brings sandwiches and lychees to a surveillance van and is not allowed in. The suspect walks out while they’re kissing against it; he makes the arrest with mustard on his cuff.
chapters.epigraph: “But I can bring lunch.”

chapters.title: The Black Box Comes to the Station
chapters.desc: Song-Zhu, newly engaged to Ren Hao, brings a phone recovered from the harbour, and the glacier works with someone who talks faster than Isla. She takes nineteen of his ten minutes.
chapters.epigraph: “I married one.”

chapters.title: Vancouver at Christmas
chapters.desc: He meets the snow, her parents in person, and a moose-shaped biscuit. He overhears Song-Zhu ask the professors how to propose to their son, and tells no one. Her childhood bedroom: explicit and silent.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s only a matter of time.”

extras.title: No Signal
extras.line: Lima, three days after the ground moved. He’s asleep at last. His phone never changed to her time.

extras.title: Paragraph Seventeen
extras.line: Five evenings at the desk while she thinks it’s overtime. Three pages, seventeen numbered paragraphs.

descs.en: The boy next door followed her to university and stayed “unofficial” for years. She loves him. She just doesn’t know how to go from friends to forever.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Eliana Lin and Wang Yu Chen grew up next door to each other in the Walled City, with a knee-high wall between their front steps. On the night she finishes school she can’t sleep, and goes to sit on her step at two in the morning. He comes out with a blanket and sits down beside her, and somewhere before dawn he realises he’s in love with her. In the morning he turns down the better medical school in the north and follows her up the hill. He tells everyone it was the course.

She works it out in a fortnight. At Mid-Autumn she climbs onto his roof to tell him to stop hovering, and he kisses her before she’s finished the sentence. After that they’re together in secret, because that’s how she wants it.

She’s the youngest Lin, born the night her mother died, and her father can barely look at her. At night, on five screens, she cleans the family’s name out of places it shouldn’t be. Yu Chen never asks her to stop. He brings tea.

Friends to lovers · Boy next door · Secret relationship · He waits · Complete in four volumes, plus twenty-two side stories

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Eliana has been in the corner of every Lin book: asleep under a ladder, filming everyone’s kisses, opening a phone in under four minutes. I kept wondering who was waiting for her on the kerb when she got home.

Yu Chen looks like the clean one, and mostly he is. But he reads her food orders every night because they’re on his card, he chose his medical school because of her, and once he lied to the cousin who raised him. The book doesn’t tell him off. In seven years he never once asks her to be someone else. He makes more tea.

Nobody cheats, and nothing hangs on a misunderstanding. They get together early, and their first times are shy and funny, because he researches everything and she wrecks the plan.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers.

A gentle, funny friends-to-lovers romance, with some hard moments:

• Love scenes on the page

• A mother who died giving birth, and a father’s coldness towards the daughter she left

• The heroine’s secret work for a crime syndicate

• A sister abducted; trafficking referred to but not shown

• A nineteen-year-old’s death in an emergency department

• Threatening messages and photographs from strangers

• A cyber-attack, a crowd crush and a crushed leg

• An attack with a broken bottle

• A partner who reads her food orders to know when she hasn’t eaten, shown without judgement

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Yu-er — Eliana's family name. Her sisters use it when they want something. Yu Chen uses it all the time, and it's the only time it comes without a favour attached.
The tall house — the Lin family house in the Walled City: old, narrow, too many stairs, a red door, and three front steps under a small tiled roof.
The porch — those three steps, with the crack in the third one, where everything that matters between them happens at two in the morning. From 2026 it runs the width of both houses.
The old Song house — next door to the Lins. Yu Chen's uncle's house, which he bought from Wei Long; later rebuilt with one long room and two desks facing each other.
The persimmon tree — in the Song garden. Its best branch hangs over the Lin side, so by old neighbourly rule its fruit are Lin persimmons. Ripe every October.
The jar — a plum-jam jar of Nainai's, kept behind a loose brick in the garden wall under the persimmon branch. Notes go in it. You don't read one until the writer has gone inside.
The Eraser — what the Syndicate calls Eliana, because she erases the Lin family's footprints. She hates the name.
The fence — what she built in October 2022, after her sister was taken: a watch on the family's names, faces and addresses that wakes her wherever she is. Two short buzzes mean family.
FENCE — her own security firm, from March 2026, in two rooms above a dumpling shop on Terrace Road. For the first month the sign was a sticky note: FENCE. Legal. Mostly.
The Spreadsheet — Eliana's record of every family secret, kept for years. "You're on a spreadsheet" is a warning.
DRAW (OFFICIAL) — Eliana's caption on the video of the paper twins' birthday party at Fig Tree Lane. Raiden contests it every year.
Red egg — a boiled egg dyed red, a traditional birthday gift. One is left at Eliana's door before dawn every 18 February. She thinks for years she knows who leaves it.
Study room 4B — the quiet room at the end of the library's fourth floor, booked to "Wang Y.C." every weekday morning since March 2022. Nobody has ever found out how.
Graduate-entry medicine — a four-year medical degree for students who already have a first degree. Yu Chen's, at the university on the hill, 2021 to 2025.
OSCE — the practical part of medical finals: timed stations with examiners and actors playing patients.
Mid-Autumn — the harvest festival at the full moon of the eighth lunar month: mooncakes, family dinners and lanterns. Every year Yu Chen puts a white rabbit lantern on his roof.
PLAN — Yu Chen's plans, in capitals, on small squares of paper. PLAN, PLAN B, PLAN C. She wrecks every one.
Nainai — grandmother on the father's side. Yu Chen's lives in the north and has had a letter from him every month for years.
The Lins, the Wangs and the Songs — Yu Chen's father was a Wang from the north, the younger brother of Xing Yue's father. His mother was a Song, Wei Long's aunt, which is how he came to live in the old Song house next door to the Lins.

chapters.title: The Boy Next Door Who Never Left
chapters.desc: The night she finishes school, Eliana can’t sleep and goes to sit on her front step at two in the morning. Yu Chen brings his blanket out and sits with her, and before it gets light he works out that he’s in love with her.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to talk. I’ll just sit here. That’s allowed.”

chapters.title: Two Gowns, Eventually
chapters.desc: First day on the hill. Eliana starts computer science and would like to be invisible, and Yu Chen has somehow started medicine at the same university and swears it’s about the course.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s the best medical course in the country. You being here is a coincidence.”

chapters.title: The Flask, the Headphones, the Tea
chapters.desc: Ten days in, Yu Chen has her new timetable memorised and a box of the headphones she destroys every fortnight. Eliana has found out she can’t concentrate when he turns pages, which is new and annoying.
chapters.epigraph: “I bought ten pairs. Don’t argue. You go through them like socks.”

chapters.title: Mid-Autumn, on the Roof
chapters.desc: Eliana climbs onto his roof at Mid-Autumn to pick a fight, because she’s worked out he didn’t end up at her university by accident. He doesn’t deny it. He kisses her in the middle of her sentence instead.
chapters.epigraph: “Stop. You’ve been circling me since September. I’m not blind. Say it.”

chapters.title: Not Official, She Says
chapters.desc: The morning after the roof, Eliana turns up with a typed list of rules: nobody knows, and it doesn’t get a name. Yu Chen agrees to every one of them and adds one of his own.
chapters.epigraph: “Fine. No name. But I’m not going to lie and say it isn’t the best thing that’s ever happened to me.”

chapters.title: The Drawing in His Pharmacology Notes
chapters.desc: Eliana can say anything with a keyboard and nothing out loud, so she hides a drawing in his notes and tells him not to look until he’s in the library. He looks in the library and has to walk out into the rain.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t look at it till you’re in the library. If you look on the bus I’ll know, because you go red on buses.”

chapters.title: He Researched This Part Too
chapters.desc: Their first night together goes nothing like his plan: it’s clumsy and shy, they keep laughing, and they start over twice. Afterwards, in the dark, he says the thing she’s most scared of so that she doesn’t have to.
chapters.epigraph: “I love you. You don’t have to say it back. I just didn’t want to be the only one who knew.”

chapters.title: He Already Knew
chapters.desc: After a bad job, Eliana finally tells him what she does at night, and finds out he’s known the outline since the summer: the nights she doesn’t eat, the light still on at four. She’s furious, and then she isn’t. He never once asks her to stop.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to ask you to stop. I’m going to keep feeding you. That’s all.”

chapters.title: The Second Winter
chapters.desc: The heating in the tall house breaks, and Eliana is sent to Zhao’s for the weekend after her father turns down Yu Chen’s offer of a warm room next door. They get through the weekend by text, and on Sunday night they meet at the garden wall.
chapters.epigraph: “He said no to my house. He didn’t say anything about the wall.”

chapters.title: Nineteen, and Nobody Says It
chapters.desc: On her birthday her father takes the family to the grave at dawn and won’t look at her, and there’s a red egg at her door like every year. That night Yu Chen gives her a whole sky to herself.
chapters.epigraph: “They wouldn’t let me bring a cake in. I asked. So you’ve got the ceiling instead.”

chapters.title: She Breaks a System for Fun
chapters.desc: Someone has been inside the wall Eliana built, fixed the one mistake she didn’t know she’d made, and sent a bill for it. Eliana has never been beaten before. She takes it badly, so Yu Chen turns it into a dare.
chapters.epigraph: “She fixed my mistake and sent a bill. A bill. One day I’m going to beat her.”

chapters.title: Useless Advice at a Birthday Lunch
chapters.desc: At Raiden and Evangeline’s birthday lunch, Yu Chen asks Raiden how to get on Lin Jian’s good side. The advice is useless, Eliana overhears it, and by the end both men are sworn to silence by a girl with a spreadsheet.
chapters.epigraph: “You want to date my sister. I want to go on living. I think we can help each other.”

chapters.title: A Hackathon, Allegedly
chapters.desc: He takes her to his family’s house by the sea for a weekend, and everyone at home thinks it’s a coding retreat. Wei Long, who raised him, rings twice with terrible advice. Nobody does any coding.
chapters.epigraph: “Bring fruit. Don’t talk about her father. Actually, don’t talk at all — you talk too much when you’re nervous.”

chapters.title: The Fence
chapters.desc: Evangeline disappears from the flower market and comes back changed, and Eliana, who can find anyone, couldn’t find her in time. Afterwards she builds something to watch for the Lin name, and won’t tell even Yu Chen what it’s for.
chapters.epigraph: “I was three days too slow. It won’t happen again. That’s all I can tell you.”

chapters.title: The Detective Already Knows
chapters.desc: Wei Long has worked out that the person the Syndicate calls “the Eraser” is the girl next door, the one the boy he raised is seeing. He comes to the garden wall off the record, to decide what to do about her, and to ask Yu Chen about a lie.
chapters.epigraph: “I asked you to your face. You looked at me and you lied. I raised you better than that. Or exactly that well.”

chapters.title: He Held the Ladder
chapters.desc: For Elowen’s flower-shop wedding, Eliana strings a sky of lights and won’t say why. The night before, a lanky boy holds her ladder for hours and slips out before anyone finds her asleep. At the wedding Raiden says “my wife” out loud, and nobody introduces the boy next door to anyone.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ll hold it. You do the stars. Don’t look down — you never look down.”

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.desc: At nineteen minutes past three in the morning, the fence catches the one thing it was built to catch. By ten she’s home and hollowed out, and the boy next door is on the kerb with his bicycle, because he always is.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to be scared on your own. That part’s mine. You can give me that part.”

chapters.title: The Night He Lost One
chapters.desc: On a Friday night in the emergency department, Yu Chen does chest compressions on a nineteen-year-old delivery rider, and nothing works. At two in the morning Eliana finds him on the east stairwell, and she stays until the sun comes up.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to say the right thing. You just don’t leave. I learned that from you.”

chapters.title: The Criminal Mind
chapters.desc: Eliana goes to a seminar to understand the men she hunts at night, and comes out with friends: a psychology student who never stops talking, her two sisters, and a cold profiler who looks at her half a second too long. Outside, Yu Chen breaks one of her rules.
chapters.epigraph: “I went to learn about monsters. I came home with a group chat.”

chapters.title: The Boy Next Door, He Always Waits
chapters.desc: A bank wants Eliana quiet, so her family sends Serafina’s fiancé to drive her to her own talk. Nobody tells Yu Chen anything. He’s on the kerb by half past five anyway, and at two in the morning he stops pretending there’s no name for what they are.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody. The boy next door. He always waits.”

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.desc: She doesn’t answer him. She doesn’t leave, either. For nine days they live on either side of a garden wall and say nothing that matters, until she knocks on his door at two in the morning.
chapters.epigraph: “Teach me forever”

chapters.title: In Front of Everyone
chapters.desc: After nine days and a knock at two in the morning, Eliana does the bravest thing she can think of. She holds his hand on the hill, in daylight, where the whole university can see. It takes her the entire walk to the gates.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m only brave for six hundred metres.”

chapters.title: Two Gowns
chapters.desc: On the same afternoon, in the same hall, Eliana gets a degree in computer science and Yu Chen gets one in medicine, which was the point of four years of “coincidence”. On the steps afterwards she kisses him in front of both families.
chapters.epigraph: “You can stop now. Elara. You can stop.”

chapters.title: The Neighbour and the Cold Gaze
chapters.desc: At the first Sunday lunch after graduation, Lin Jian tells the table, and not his daughter, that she won’t be wasting a Lin future on a policeman’s nephew. Yu Chen, who has never raised his voice in that house, stands up.
chapters.epigraph: “Wanting your father to love you isn’t a weakness.”

chapters.title: A Job Offer and a Night Shift
chapters.desc: Her father summons her to the fishing-net building, where the Syndicate offers her the Syndicate’s top security post, full time, for life. The same night Yu Chen works his first night as a real doctor, and she takes dinner up to the top of the car park.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t take a thing just because somebody’s finally decided you’re worth keeping.”

chapters.title: The Breach
chapters.desc: For the first time in her life, someone gets through Eliana’s walls — a crew called Magpie, let in by an old key she handed out herself in second year. It isn’t just data. It’s the family’s safe-house addresses, and a clock starts.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re not on your own in this room”

chapters.title: Thirty-Six Hours
chapters.desc: She doesn’t sleep for a day and a half, hunting the crew that holds her family’s addresses. Yu Chen doesn’t leave. When she finds them, the choice is hers: give it to her father, who would make them vanish, or hand it to the law.
chapters.epigraph: “You didn’t give me a file, or ask me to make anything disappear. You asked me to help you bring it into the light.”

chapters.title: Someone Else’s Blood
chapters.desc: The breach turns physical. A man is sent to frighten Eliana at the dawn flower market, the crowd breaks, and a stallholder is crushed under a van. Yu Chen is there, off duty, and Eliana sees for the first time exactly what he chose to do with his life, and what else his hands can do.
chapters.epigraph: “Same job. Two sides of a wall.”

chapters.title: The First Child to Say No to His Face
chapters.desc: At the Mid-Autumn table, with the whole family watching, Lin Jian announces the job as a thing already decided. Eliana turns it down, and him, out loud and to his face. Nobody in the house has ever done that before.
chapters.epigraph: “But not wanting something is enough not to give my life to it.”

chapters.title: The Eldest Sister Takes Her Side
chapters.desc: The eldest sister comes to the tall house and says to their father the thing the family has let him avoid for twenty-two years. It doesn’t mend him. But it makes him stop, and that evening, on the roof next door, Eliana says she’s leaving.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re not leaving your family. And you’re not losing your home. You’re choosing another one.”

chapters.title: Two Boxes and a Monitor
chapters.desc: Eliana moves out of the tall house where she’s lived at the top of the stairs in the dark. It takes two boxes, a suitcase of hard drives and one monitor. He carries the monitor. She doesn’t go far, only next door, which was always where she was going.
chapters.epigraph: “Now you can just turn over.”

chapters.title: The Red Egg
chapters.desc: The first February she wakes up next door, there’s still a red egg on the step, and this time she catches who leaves it. At the grave at dawn her father turns to her and says the words. That night she writes one word on a sticky note and puts it in Yu Chen’s textbook.
chapters.epigraph: “It was always me.”

chapters.title: Legal, Mostly
chapters.desc: Eliana opens her own security firm in two rooms above a dumpling shop, with a sticky note for a sign. Si-Wei writes the business plan. Yu Chen bought the building a week ago and mentions it on opening night, which goes about as well as he expected.
chapters.epigraph: “That’s what Baba does.”

chapters.title: The First Client Is Very Loud
chapters.desc: FENCE’s first real client is Ren Hao, who hires Eliana at top volume, hugs everyone in the building and says “I love you” to the dumpling woman. Two weeks later, at Serafina’s wedding, Eliana leaves early with cake, because Yu Chen is on nights.
chapters.epigraph: “Ren Hao can say it to the whole building. I put it in your textbook.”

chapters.title: He Matches to Emergency Medicine
chapters.desc: Yu Chen is offered emergency medicine training at City Hospital, the first thing in years he has chosen entirely for himself. He doesn’t know how to say it out loud. Eliana throws him the loudest party a quiet person can stand.
chapters.epigraph: “Making your life smaller before I’ve even asked you to.”

chapters.title: Three Flats and a Porch
chapters.desc: They look at three new flats with harbour views and buy none of them. Instead they rebuild the old Song house as theirs, keep the porch, and take down the little wall between the two porches, which needs her father’s permission and costs him more than he lets show.
chapters.epigraph: “Old because we chose to keep them.”

chapters.title: Nainai
chapters.desc: Yu Chen takes Eliana north to meet the grandmother he has written to every month for years. Nainai has kept every letter, has known Eliana’s name since the summer of 2021, and before they leave she gives him his mother’s ring.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t mind that you loved me. I mind if you forget I’m allowed to go.”

chapters.title: The Ring in the Jar
chapters.desc: After the hillclimb, and after a night in the emergency department when she nearly loses him, Eliana leaves a note in the jar in the wall: “Ask me again.” He does, at two in the morning, on the porch where it started, with his mother’s ring.
chapters.epigraph: “Ask me again.”

chapters.title: A Wedding Between Two Gardens
chapters.desc: They marry where they both lived for years, across both back gardens, under the persimmon tree, through a gate cut in the wall. She means to walk to him on her own. At the gate her father is waiting, and for the first time in her life he asks her something.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ll come out. Every night.”

chapters.title: 2 A.M., The Porch
chapters.desc: Epilogue. On the night she turns twenty-five, Eliana sits on the porch at two in the morning, not because the house is too quiet but because it’s exactly quiet enough. She has something to ask. The boy next door comes out and sits down beside her.
chapters.epigraph: “I just want to keep finding you.”

chapters.title: A History of Untangled Headphones
chapters.desc: Six years of Yu Chen untangling Eliana’s wired headphones, mending the ones she breaks, and buying the last forty pairs in the city when the make is stopped. He has never once complained. Then she finds the one pair she untangled for him.
chapters.epigraph: “A lifetime.”

chapters.title: The Library Booking System
chapters.desc: Study room 4B has been booked to “Wang Y.C.” every Friday since the March of his first year, and nobody has ever beaten him to it. The librarian who has watched it for four years has her suspicions. She never finds out how.
chapters.epigraph: “For the librarian who kept our mornings safe.”

chapters.title: The Sticky Note Drawer
chapters.desc: Every note Eliana was ever too shy to say out loud, kept in order in a drawer in Yu Chen’s desk, from a smiling dumpling in her first fortnight on the hill to the one that just said “Official”. The week before the wedding, she catches him reading them.
chapters.epigraph: “Some things are nice when they’re kept.”

chapters.title: A Background Check on Her Best Friend’s Boyfriend
chapters.desc: When her best friend says, in four words, that she’s seeing Geum Sung Jae, who runs the Iron Dogs in the grey market behind the old dockyard, Eliana does what a good friend does: a thorough, unasked-for background check, three times, overnight. She finds nothing she can prove, which annoys her more than anything else could.
chapters.epigraph: “Because the first two times I didn’t find anything.”

chapters.title: The Security Flaw Rematch
chapters.desc: Four years after He Si-Mei fixed her mistake and sent a bill, Eliana finally gets her in the same room: a legal contest on the thirty-second floor of Ren Hao’s firm, with signed rules and Professor Szeto keeping score. Eleven hours later the board says draw. Neither of them believes it.
chapters.epigraph: “It’ll be there when you’ve beaten her.”

chapters.title: Neither of Them Can Cook
chapters.desc: Two clever people who live on instant noodles and whatever Auntie Tsoi leaves decide to make dumplings from scratch for the whole family’s Sunday lunch. By eleven o’clock they have a plan, a spreadsheet and something that has to be hidden in the oven and later buried in the garden.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re clever people. You can learn to fold a dumpling.”

chapters.title: The Sisters’ Group Chat
chapters.desc: Eliana is the admin, which means she runs the sisters’ group chat with an iron hand, adds Haozhen once for a joke, adds Raiden for a worse one, and removes Raiden whenever he gets back in. Three years of a family, told one message at a time.
chapters.epigraph: “I knew you loved him. That was enough.”

chapters.title: A Notebook of Teas, All for Her
chapters.desc: Yu Chen keeps a notebook of teas, every one worked out for one of Eliana’s bad nights: can’t sleep, won’t eat, nine hours at a screen. It’s a love letter he’d never call one. One page near the back isn’t in his handwriting.
chapters.epigraph: “Sometimes she only needs somewhere to put her hands.”

chapters.title: The Monitor Wall
chapters.desc: On the night they graduate, Eliana takes Yu Chen up to her room to show him what she does all night, and he tries, once, to understand her five screens so he can help. He doesn’t. But he learns which chair, and which hour, and that turns out to be the help.
chapters.epigraph: “Which hour’s the worst?”

chapters.title: The Boy Who Brought His Blanket
chapters.desc: On their first wedding anniversary Eliana comes home from a job abroad, takes his mother’s old cream blanket out of the cupboard and tells Yu Chen what she was really doing on the steps that June night in 2021, the night she finished school, when he came out and sat down beside her and she fell asleep on his arm. Or didn’t.
chapters.epigraph: “I wasn’t dreaming. I didn’t want you to go.”

chapters.title: Before the Persimmons Were Ripe
chapters.desc: Lin Jian waited outside a dried-goods shop for six evenings before Qi Wanqing came out and laughed at him. This is how he loved her: the persimmon branch, a registry in 1987, the kitchen chair where she said no, a lemon tree, two children in one week, a girl from Plum Steps, red eggs he could never dye properly, and the hospital corridor where he lost her.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to look frightening in here”

chapters.title: The First New Year With Everyone Married
chapters.desc: For the first time, all five Lin children come home for New Year with the people they married. Ah Sim rules the kitchen, the husbands weigh their red envelopes, Raiden makes a toast nobody asked for, and after the fish their father says their mother’s name.
chapters.epigraph: “At least nobody’s missing.”

chapters.title: All Four on the Same Night
chapters.desc: Yu Chen is the emergency registrar on nights, his cousin Xing Yue is the surgeon on call, Elara brings a transfer from Harbourside, and Wei Long stands outside theatre with a prisoner. At three Eliana arrives with five boxes of noodles. At four a man comes into the department with a knife.
chapters.epigraph: “That’s why I’m choosing to.”

chapters.title: The Lin Family Weekend, Part One: Arrivals
chapters.desc: Elowen and Zhao host every Lin child and every husband and wife for the Mid-Autumn weekend, in a house with an armoury and a panic room under the tulips. Raiden brings a floor plan with the rooms wrong. Zhao says one word to each husband. Eliana arrives late because she rewired the gate.
chapters.epigraph: “Because you drew it.”

chapters.title: The Lin Family Weekend, Part Two: The Wives’ Kitchen, the Husbands’ Lawn
chapters.desc: The women take the kitchen and the men are sent out to make the barbecue. Inside, the wives tell each other the most romantic thing and the most frightening thing their husbands have done. Outside, five men stand round a fire, and Jun Hyuk asks what each of them would do if someone hurt his wife.
chapters.epigraph: “And then I’d stitch him afterwards.”

chapters.title: The Lin Family Weekend, Part Three: Who Knows Their Spouse Best
chapters.desc: Eliana builds a buzzer, writes a spreadsheet and makes Raiden the host. Five couples answer questions about each other with Baba as judge, and the answers reveal a year remembered for a noodle order, a tea notebook, a forty-minute search and the exact morning someone changed her mind.
chapters.epigraph: “I married you. I knew what I was getting.”

chapters.title: The Lin Family Weekend, Part Four: The Mall
chapters.desc: Five husbands are sent to the biggest shopping centre in the city to buy the dinner and one present each, alone, while five wives follow them with binoculars. Zhao stands in a florist’s for twenty-one minutes, Yu Chen rings Jinx about headphones, and on an escalator all five men become exactly who they are in three seconds.
chapters.epigraph: “She wants the old ones to last forever.”

chapters.title: The Lin Family Weekend, Part Five: Lanterns on the Lawn
chapters.desc: Lanterns on the lawn, mooncakes from Auntie Au, thirteen small lanterns with thirteen names, and a nine-word speech from Baba. Raiden finally gets his photograph. Ah Sim and Uncle Mok share their mother’s green flask on the bench by the lemon tree.
chapters.epigraph: “Your mother wanted a big table. Here it is.”

chapters.title: Terrible Advice From the Cousin Who Raised Him
chapters.desc: In 2022 Wei Long tells Yu Chen to tell Eliana everything he wants, and Yu Chen doesn’t. In 2025, after the nine days, Wei Long asks him about a consular officer who sits on his desk, and gets his own advice back. Eliana hears both from the garden wall.
chapters.epigraph: “I know what happens when you don’t.”

chapters.title: He Joins the Family Chat
chapters.desc: Eliana adds her father to Lins + Strays. After forty minutes he sends one word. Every morning at six there’s another, and the family learns to answer a man who means far more than he types, until her birthday the next year, when he sends four.
chapters.epigraph: “Breakfast at seven. Your favourite.”

chapters.title: Ah Sim’s Gate
chapters.desc: The red door in the back wall of the Lin house, told by the woman who has kept its key since Qi Wanqing gave it to her in 1987: a girl from Plum Steps, a boy with a map on his arm, a daughter-in-law told to sit down, a step scrubbed clean, and a girl who always preferred the wall.
chapters.epigraph: “Sometimes it’s the only way they know how to come home.”

chapters.title: Every Eighteenth of February
chapters.desc: Twenty-five dawns at Qi Wanqing’s grave, one each year from the first after she died to Eliana’s twenty-fifth birthday: who came, who didn’t, what their father said and didn’t say, and the red egg left at Eliana’s door every year by someone she never saw.
chapters.epigraph: “The day was hers, too.”

extras.title: Since Summer
extras.line: The night she tells him what she does. He already knew. She reads his phone while he washes her bowl.

extras.title: Lin Yu
extras.line: A blanket on a wet wall, a red egg, a sky with her other name on it, and someone who says hi inside her config.

descs.en: He thinks her hands are broken and opens every door for her. She secretly got her surgeon’s hands back, and works nights in a basement as the family’s ghost surgeon.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Elara Lin is a final-year medical student who talks all the time, practises stitches on bananas, and on her first morning on the surgical ward tells the chief resident he’s missed a leak. She’s right. By the evening Wang Xing Yue has handed her logbook to someone else, so that he’s allowed to ask her to dinner.

She’s also the Lins’ surgeon. When the family’s people bleed somewhere a hospital can’t see, she goes. In a supply room at three in the morning she begs him not to ask, and he promises he won’t.

He keeps that promise through a knife at her father’s door, a winter when she stops talking, and the year she gets her hands back in secret and goes to work in a cellar, in a mask, as Doctor Ghost. He never asks her to stop. He restocks her bag.

He falls first · Doctors in love · Married early · Complete in four volumes, plus ten side stories

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Elara has been in the corner of every Lin book: late, in scrubs, crying at weddings, running a county hospital in her Saturday jeans. I wanted to know what that cost her, and who looks after the person who looks after everyone.

Xing Yue isn’t a nice man to anyone but her. He tracks her phone, goes through her bag and lies to his own professor without blinking, and the book doesn’t tell him off for it. The one thing he never does is ask her to be someone else.

There’s blood, because it’s a book about surgeons, but the medicine stays at story level. They get a long kitchen, two pagers and a phone in a drawer that rings at half past eleven.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers.

A warm, funny medical romance, with some hard moments:

• Love scenes on the page, from early on

• Knife and gunshot wounds, and surgery outside hospitals with stolen supplies

• A people-smuggling boat and its frightened survivors

• Burns after a fire

• A knife attack and a serious hand injury

• Nerve pain, withdrawal into silence, and the truth about how her birth parents died

• A fire that kills two people, and a killing at the harbour wall

• A girl’s face cut with a bottle

• A suspension at work

• A footbridge collapse with many casualties

• A partner who tracks her phone and goes through her bag, shown without judgement

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
City Hospital — the teaching hospital at the foot of the hill. Ward 9B, general surgery, is on the ninth floor of the tower; the old 1930s block stands behind it.
Harbourside General — the big hospital by the harbour, where Elara does her intern year and goes back to training in 2027.
The Crestview — the private hospital on the hill above the old racecourse, which asks no questions of people who pay, and where Ms. Cui makes her cry.
The hospital garden — behind the old block: a camphor tree older than the hospital, a koi pond, and the fourth window along on the first floor, which was her mother's ward.
14 Banyan Terrace — his flat, the top two floors and roof of a white 1950s building ten minutes downhill from City Hospital.
2 Camphor Hill — the old doctor's house above the hospital, with a long kitchen and a back room for the rig. Bought in both their names, without asking.
The Walled City — the old district where the Lins live, behind a red door with a brass fish knocker and eleven chairs that don't match.
The cellar under the rope store — the room Raiden builds next to the garage near the Docks, behind a steel door painted to look like wood.
Doctor Ghost — the name the docks give the masked surgeon who never speaks and always hums.
The rig — Jinx's steel training machine for Elara's hand: a forearm cradle, pulleys, a turntable and a fine wire that whispers until her hand is where she sent it.
The ghost phone — the line that rings only from her father's or Uncle Mok's numbers. From July 2027 it lives in the kitchen drawer.
The dot — her phone location, shared with him ‘for night shifts’ from 2023, and his with her from 2026.
The rules — what they wrote on the back of his suspension letter. Rule one: nobody does this alone.
Qu Xiaoyue — her birth name, ‘little moon’. Elara is a moon of Jupiter, so she kept a piece of it.
Qu Lighterage — her father's firm: four lighter boats between the ships and the old Walled City piers.
Plum Steps — the children's home at the top of a long flight of stone steps, closed in 2011.
Loupes — magnifying glasses surgeons wear to operate. Hers are dark red, made for her eyes, with E.L. inside the arm.
Registrar, consultant — a registrar is a mid-level surgeon in training; a consultant is the senior surgeon in charge.

chapters.title: The Student Who Told the Chief Resident He Was Wrong
chapters.desc: On her first morning in surgery, a final-year student tells the chief resident he’s missed a leak. She’s right, and he has seen her face before.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d rather be wrong about this one.”

chapters.title: Love at First Sight Is a Sleep-Deprivation Symptom
chapters.desc: Elara finds her logbook handed to someone else and marches into the chief resident’s office to apologise for being right. He tells her why, and it isn’t a question.
chapters.epigraph: “I can’t take you to dinner and sign your logbook. I picked dinner.”

chapters.title: Suturing Practice on a Banana
chapters.desc: She beats every student in the skills lab with a needle and a banana. At dinner she talks for three hours, and on the steps outside he stops her in the middle of a story.
chapters.epigraph: “Finish the story later.”

chapters.title: She Narrates Everything
chapters.desc: A month of noodles at eleven and slow walks to the taxi rank. Then she turns up at his flat with breakfast after his night on call, and doesn’t go home.
chapters.epigraph: “I thought it was sleep deprivation. I gave it fifteen months.”

chapters.title: The Lins Are Not Told
chapters.desc: For her twenty-third birthday he gives her surgical loupes made for her eyes. She goes to the family dinner without him, and climbs into his car at midnight still in her dress.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re the one part of my life nobody’s ever bled on.”

chapters.title: Three in the Morning, on Speaker
chapters.desc: Her silent sister rings from a strange phone about a man with an infected knife wound who can’t go to a hospital. For three weeks Elara calls back at three every morning, and Xing Yue writes it all down and never asks who.
chapters.epigraph: “Go back to sleep. I’ve written it down.”

chapters.title: A Bullet on the Hill
chapters.desc: Her sister’s husband crawls home with a bullet in his side, and Elara steals what she needs from the hospital. Xing Yue walks into the supply room and catches her, and she begs him not to ask.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t ask me. If you ask, I’ll tell you.”

chapters.title: Fifteen Days of Drips
chapters.desc: For two weeks she changes drips and dressings on the hill, and he drives her there in the dark and waits at the bottom of the road. On the last night he asks one question.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not asking who. I only want to know if he’s alive.”

chapters.title: Every Wrong Answer
chapters.desc: Finals, flashcards in bed and a dare he cheats on. She graduates with her family in the hall, and on the back stairs afterwards he hands her a form already filled in, and she says yes in the middle of a sentence.
chapters.epigraph: “Get it wrong and I’ll kiss you anyway.”

chapters.title: The Flat on Banyan Terrace
chapters.desc: She starts as an intern across the harbour, living out of a bag, and he hands her the key to a room he’s already finished. She picks the date. On a Friday morning in the old town they marry in secret, with a retired bus driver and a night sister for witnesses.
chapters.epigraph: “Now that’s an answer.”

chapters.title: The Cake
chapters.desc: Elara makes four tiers of cake for Elowen’s wedding, and the tall doctor in glasses stands beside it all night while nobody introduces him. At midnight her father asks his name, and he tells him: her husband.
chapters.epigraph: “Sunday. One o’clock. Bring him.”

chapters.title: Sunday Lunch in the Walled City
chapters.desc: The red door, eleven chairs and a father who has learned to ask things. Raiden asks his intentions, and Xing Yue tells the whole table he’s already married her.
chapters.epigraph: “Does she eat when she’s on nights?”

chapters.title: His Brother Comes for Tea
chapters.desc: Elara finds out her silent sister got married before she did, and told nobody either. Then his brother flies down for one cup of tea, notices everything, and lets slip how rich the Wangs really are.
chapters.epigraph: “He rang me to ask whether love at first sight was in the literature.”

chapters.title: He Is Bad at Holidays
chapters.desc: He works every holiday so other people can go home. On Lunar New Year’s Eve his wife brings dumplings to Ward 9B, and he breaks his own rule.
chapters.epigraph: “I said not in the hospital. I’m allowed to be wrong.”

chapters.title: Ring Me First
chapters.desc: Her sister shoots a man in a noodle shop, and Elara runs across the road from the bakery and takes over a county hospital. She gets home at midnight and shakes on the hall floor, and her husband asks for names.
chapters.epigraph: “Next time ring me first. I’ll drive. I’ll wait in the car.”

chapters.title: The Vow at Dawn
chapters.desc: On the morning she finishes her intern year he meets her in the old garden at City Hospital and asks his wife to marry him again, in front of everyone this time. She’s talking about fish, and says yes in the middle of a sentence.
chapters.epigraph: “Sorry, what? Say it again. I was talking.”

chapters.title: The Seventh Guest
chapters.desc: Elara kneels in a noodle shop’s back room by the river after midnight while her husband waits in the car, then runs late up a lane in scrubs to her sister’s garden wedding. That night she says she doesn’t know who her own mother was.
chapters.epigraph: “Ev knows who her mother was now.”

chapters.title: A Name in a Ledger
chapters.desc: He finds the old matron of the children’s home and the birth name his wife has never heard. He decides to keep it for their garden day, and she catches him hiding something.
chapters.epigraph: “They called her the bell girl. She never stopped.”

chapters.title: Again?
chapters.desc: At five in the morning her brother and his wife come in from a fire with burned hands. For six weeks she spends her days off fixing switches in the rebuilt shop, humming, and her husband catches her on a ladder.
chapters.epigraph: “You’ve got good hands. Steady. I’d hire you.”

chapters.title: The Knife at the Red Door
chapters.desc: After Sunday lunch a man in a seaman’s jacket comes for her father with a knife. Elara gets in the way, and her husband keeps her alive on the stones of the alley, then stands in the corner of theatre with empty hands.
chapters.epigraph: “Stop diagnosing yourself. I know what’s cut.”

chapters.title: The House Is Too Quiet
chapters.desc: Lin Jian tells her where she came from and what he did. She finds out Xing Yue has known her name for nine months, and stops talking to everyone.
chapters.epigraph: “It was mine. You picked the day.”

chapters.title: She Gives the Ring Back
chapters.desc: Out of the splint, Elara puts the ring in his hand and goes to stay with the sister who knows what it is to learn why you were kept. He sits on the porch step every night for five weeks.
chapters.epigraph: “Keep it safe. I’m not giving it to anybody else.”

chapters.title: The Machine Before the Garage Opens
chapters.desc: At five every morning, before the garage opens, Elara works her ruined hand on a steel rig Jinx built for her. Her uncle pleads guilty, and she watches from the gallery.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m writing so that you know I survived. I’m here.”

chapters.title: Her Mother’s Window
chapters.desc: In a prison visiting room her uncle gives her the only photographs of her parents. She finds her mother’s ward window over the hospital garden, and Xing Yue asks her again.
chapters.epigraph: “She sang. When she was doing things.”

chapters.title: A Surgeon Who Doesn’t Exist
chapters.desc: At one in the morning her father rings for the first time in eight months: his driver’s grandson is bleeding on the kitchen table. Elara picks up the instruments herself, and her hands don’t shake.
chapters.epigraph: “I won’t forget your rules.”

chapters.title: The Cellar Under the Rope Store
chapters.desc: Raiden opens a room under the old rope store next to the garage, and Evangeline comes to hand her the instruments. The ghost never says a word.
chapters.epigraph: “Then I won’t. Not down here. Not one word.”

chapters.title: The Pillowcase
chapters.desc: He wakes at two in the morning to find her sewing up a torn pillowcase by the light of her phone. He knows a surgeon’s hands when he sees them, and a week later he follows her to a steel door.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s a pillowcase. Don’t look at it like a specimen.”

chapters.title: Notes in the Margins
chapters.desc: He starts leaving surgical journals open on the kitchen table at the hardest cases. She can’t resist writing in the margins, and he answers.
chapters.epigraph: “Good. I like who I’m turning into.”

chapters.title: Doctor Ghost
chapters.desc: A young man on a trolley hears Elara humming and calls her Doctor Ghost. Xing Yue frightens him quiet, lies in the notes, goes through her black bag in the night, and buys her instruments she thanks her sister for.
chapters.epigraph: “Then make it somewhere she can tell you things.”

chapters.title: Two Surgeons, One Table
chapters.desc: Zhao’s guard is shot at the armory gate and is bleeding faster than one surgeon can stop. Elara writes the call she swore she’d never make, and her husband comes down the steps in thirteen minutes with two units of blood in his own name.
chapters.epigraph: “He says he knows where it is. He says thirteen minutes.”

chapters.title: I Know
chapters.desc: The blood bank finds two missing units with his name on them and he’s suspended, and he tells her nothing. She finds the letter, and he tells her he’s known since the pillowcase.
chapters.epigraph: “I never loved you for your hands.”

chapters.title: Rules for a Ghost Surgeon
chapters.desc: They write the ghost’s rules together on the back of his suspension letter. Then he takes her north for New Year, where his grandmother points her stick at everyone.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody does this alone.”

chapters.title: No More Pretending
chapters.desc: At Lunar New Year, in the middle of Raiden’s toast, Elara picks up her teacup with one hand. Then she tells the whole table.
chapters.epigraph: “Next time tell me badly.”

chapters.title: He Goes Back to Work
chapters.desc: The review gives him a warning and his job back. She walks him to the hospital gate in a banana cap, sets the date under her mother’s window, and finds out he’s bought a house without asking.
chapters.epigraph: “Like a very distinguished fruit.”

chapters.title: The Skills Test
chapters.desc: A hand surgeon she’s never met tests her strength and feeling, and examiners time her on a model bowel. He isn’t allowed in, so he waits in the car park for three hours.
chapters.epigraph: “Well. You’re here.”

chapters.title: The Board Asks About the Accident
chapters.desc: At her interview they ask about the knife and the year after it. She tells the truth, and when they ask the one question she won’t answer, she says so.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re beautiful at four in the morning.”

chapters.title: The Wedding Under Her Mother’s Window
chapters.desc: They marry again at six in the morning in the hospital garden, with the night staff in scrubs at the back. She talks too long, and he says one sentence.
chapters.epigraph: “Talk as long as you like.”

chapters.title: Not Under Her Husband
chapters.desc: Her first day back in surgical training is at Harbourside, under a registrar younger than she is. That night the black phone rings in their kitchen drawer, and they go together.
chapters.epigraph: “Ambulance first. Nothing a hospital should do.”

chapters.title: A Mass Casualty Night
chapters.desc: A footbridge comes down at the lantern fair, and every hospital in the city fills. Across the harbour from her husband, Elara packs a torn liver and closes her first patient on her own.
chapters.epigraph: “Being frightened doesn’t make it less yours.”

chapters.title: Twin Scrub Caps
chapters.desc: A year since the garden. Nearly five years married. Two pagers and a ghost’s phone on the kitchen counter, all quiet, and a pair of silly caps.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ve catalogued them.”

chapters.title: The First Time He Saw Her
chapters.desc: At the end of a twenty-six-hour shift he’s sent to look at a young man’s ribs, and a medical student in a T-shirt stops him by the lift to ask about her brother’s spleen.
chapters.epigraph: “Observation is a decision.”

chapters.title: Before She Had a Family Name
chapters.desc: On the morning of her wedding, Lin Jian sits at his kitchen table before dawn and remembers the autumn of 2002: a schedule sold to the wrong man, a fire he watched from across the water, and a children’s home on Plum Steps.
chapters.epigraph: “Everything has a name.”

chapters.title: A Cafeteria Lunch, Narrated
chapters.desc: Twenty minutes on the mystery meat in the hospital canteen, while the chief resident eats his and the next table watches him listen.
chapters.epigraph: “Now you’ve had some.”

chapters.title: Perfect Squares
chapters.desc: On Christmas Eve, a month after the knife, he cuts her dinner into exact squares. She tells him what she thinks of that, and then she makes him do a dumpling.
chapters.epigraph: “You killed it twice.”

chapters.title: The Cousin Who Wants Emergency Medicine
chapters.desc: Yu Chen comes to Banyan Terrace to ask his mentor about emergency medicine, and about something harder. Elara walks in talking.
chapters.epigraph: “It gets complicated when people won’t say what they mean.”

chapters.title: Banned From Trivia Night
chapters.desc: The hospital social club bans Elara from the Tuesday quiz after four weeks of her team winning. She appeals, and Xing Yue, on the other side, gets every question wrong.
chapters.epigraph: “One for each right answer.”

chapters.title: Doctor’s Orders: Nap
chapters.desc: After three nights in a row he writes her a prescription for a nap. She complies, loudly, like an operation note, and falls asleep in the middle of a sentence.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to earn the right to lie down.”

chapters.title: The Machine
chapters.desc: Jinx builds the rig at night in the workshop at Tai Hing, from calipers and graph paper and a hand she measured at Ev’s kitchen table. Then she doesn’t watch.
chapters.epigraph: “These she can do herself.”

chapters.title: Handwriting Nobody Else Can Read
chapters.desc: Nobody can read a word he writes except Elara. Pharmacists ring her to translate, and some of the notes are only for her.
chapters.epigraph: “Here is the rest of your name.”

chapters.title: The Stitches Competition
chapters.desc: At the trainees’ skills night Elara takes on her husband and his cousin with a chicken thigh each. She wins, and he asks for a rematch at home, in writing.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not made of glass.”

extras.title: Star Sapphire
extras.line: A piece of thread while she sleeps. A window on Harbour Road. One Sunday he swaps.

extras.title: Bottom Step
extras.line: Five weeks on her sister’s porch step. Tonight she came down. She asked him for everything, and he’s asleep.

descs.en: She nearly ran him over at a street race and jumped off her bike to fight him. He complimented her intake manifold.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Raiden Lin plays the cheerful, slightly useless Lin son so well that the Syndicate and the police both ignore him. In fact he draws the family’s safe rooms and knows the weak point of every building in the city.

One night he’s kneeling in the middle of an illegal race on the old shipyard road, sketching a warehouse, when a motorbike stops two metres from him. Jinx gets off to beat some sense into him. He looks up and tells her that her intake manifold is beautiful.

She grew up in a chop shop under the flyover and swore she’d never be owned by anyone, least of all a Lin. He would like to marry her. He asks on a napkin, drawn to scale. She says not yet. He keeps asking.

He falls first · Sunshine and grump · Mechanic heroine · Complete in four volumes, plus six side stories

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Raiden is the Lin who talks. In every other book he’s in the background, cheerful, drawing something, being an idiot on purpose. I wanted to know who he was when he stopped pretending, and who he would stop for. It had to be someone who could see through him at a hundred and ninety kilometres an hour.

This is the lightest book in the series, with the most kissing. They’re together by chapter three. The trouble isn’t whether they’ll fall in love. It’s her father’s debts, his father’s name, and two people who were each hidden as children learning not to hide each other.

He spoils her: a building, a dyno, a lathe, a hill. She pays half. She insisted.
