glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
The black door — Jinx's first garage, near the Iron Docks, under an old sign that says TAI HING ROPE & CANVAS.
The shipyard road — Two kilometres of cracked concrete between the dead shipyard and the cranes. Illegal races at one in the morning.
Mrs. Tong's — The noodle place on the corner that only serves men off the container ships. The table by the fridge, back to the wall.
The Meridian — Raiden's glass tower in the Symmetrical Ward. Thirty-one floors. The desk man calls the pale green bike “the tram”.
The pale green bike — The one Jinx built him. Twenty kilometres an hour, lights like a train, a drawing board on the tank, a bell.
The steel room — Behind her tool wall. A light that comes on by itself, air, a line out, a warm lamp she added, and a tin of peaches.
The napkins — Thirty-one proposals, each drawn to scale, kept in his wallet where other people keep photographs.
Under the flyover — The Slums of the Industry, where the sun never gets in. Her father's shop, CAO MOTOR REPAIR.
The gap — Behind the scrap heap, between the wall and the pillar. On the archive drawings from 1974.
The triple — A 1973 two-stroke, three cylinders, a widowmaker. Seized for seven years. Ran at 5:40 a.m.
Oh-three-one-one — The day she left. The code to everything she owns.
JINX — The shop in the old chandler's warehouse three doors down, with a long low window anyone can see into. The sign she cut herself.
The stair — Behind the third shelf on the mezzanine. Two hours of fire board. Used once.
The driveway — One point two kilometres on the hill above the reservoir road. It is a racetrack.
The monkey — The passenger in a racing sidecar, who hangs off the side. Raiden says navigator.
Dyno — A rolling road that measures a bike's power at the back wheel.
Intake manifold — The pipes that carry air and fuel into the engine. Hers are all the same length, by hand.

chapters.title: Sketching in the Middle of a Race Track
chapters.desc: She nearly ran him over at a street race and jumped off her bike to fight him. He complimented her intake manifold.
chapters.epigraph: “I didn’t hit him. Write that down. I want it on record that I didn’t hit him.”

chapters.title: “Nice Intake Manifold” Is Not a Pick-Up Line
chapters.desc: He turns up at the black door with three coffees because he didn’t know how she took it. She drinks all three.
chapters.epigraph: “I brought three because I didn’t know how you took it. Now I know. You take all three.”

chapters.title: The Socialite Everyone Ignores
chapters.desc: A gallery on the fortieth floor, a man who plays the fool and counts the exits, and a confession on the fire stairs.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody shoots the boy who can’t find his own coat.”

chapters.title: The First Kiss Smells Like Oil
chapters.desc: She throws the spanner a metre wide. Under her bike, he won’t kiss her until she tells him her real name.
chapters.epigraph: “I said I’d go if you threw a spanner. I didn’t say what happens if you miss.”

chapters.title: The Van on the Way to Her
chapters.desc: Fourteen days of coffee and goodnights on her step. Then a van on the Docks road, a night at Harbourside General, and the back door.
chapters.epigraph: “I was on the pavement. I promise. I was on the pavement.”

chapters.title: A Bike That Goes Twenty Kilometres an Hour
chapters.desc: Three weeks of silence, then Zhao at her door with her jacket and two sentences. She builds a pale green bike that won’t go past twenty and rides it into his lobby.
chapters.epigraph: “If you’re going to draw in roads, you do it on this.”

chapters.title: Her Father’s Chop Shop
chapters.desc: His plaster comes off and he rides pillion for the first time. From a roof she shows him her father’s chop shop under the flyover. He goes home and maps every way out of it.
chapters.epigraph: “First word I ever read was torque.”

chapters.title: He Asks Her to Marry Him on a Napkin Drawing
chapters.desc: At Mrs. Tong’s he slides a napkin across the table with their whole life drawn on it at 1:50. She says yes, on five conditions, signed in chilli oil.
chapters.epigraph: “Yes. A registry. Not your father’s house.”

chapters.title: The Trophy Husband Has Dinner Ready
chapters.desc: The old-town registry, two washers for rings, Mrs. Tong crying louder than anyone. Then her husband moves into her two rooms with a wok.
chapters.epigraph: “Somebody has to cook. You’d put soup in a gearbox if I let you.”

chapters.title: The Roof That Will Never Fall
chapters.desc: Winter to spring. A lawyers’ letter says her building has been sold, and it has, to her. A dyno, a steel room behind the tools, a roof that won’t leak, and a napkin a month.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s in your name. Only yours. I’m sorry. I know I promised I’d only use it when it was important.”

chapters.title: The Meanest Engineer in the City
chapters.desc: A charity gala full of people who know his father, and a racing driver with kitchen-scissor hair who catches him looking at a crack. A gearbox, a dark gold bike, and a sidecar called Architect.
chapters.epigraph: “She could build a bike faster than you could crash it. I’d bet money. I’d bet your money.”

chapters.title: Proud of Her for an Entire Week
chapters.desc: Her black bike wins Best in Show up north, and her husband tells a petrol station, a toll booth and a coach party. He tells everyone except his own family.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d like everyone to know. I’d like a plane to write it in the sky. I’ve looked into it. It’s very expensive and the wind spoils the letters.”

chapters.title: Memes at 2 A.M.
chapters.desc: He sends her memes from the next pillow at two in the morning. Then he tells her about a freezer and eleven hours, and she works out what his steel room is.
chapters.epigraph: “You built me a freezer with the light on.”

chapters.title: Ten, Walking Home Alone
chapters.desc: How a boy of ten copied a road map onto his arm and crossed a border in a fish truck. At two in the morning she rides him to the red door in his father’s back wall.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody was coming. So I went to them.”

chapters.title: A Commission From the Syndicate
chapters.desc: She finds drawings on the kitchen table for a hidden steel room on the Peak road with C.S. in the corner. Their worst fight ends on the workbench, and on Monday he bolts a safe to the floor.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody looks at me. That’s the whole point.” “I looked.”

chapters.title: Meeting the Family Properly
chapters.desc: Elowen’s wedding in the flower shop. “This is Jinx. My wife.” Thirty people go silent, Lin Jian walks out into the street, and she goes after him.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ve always wondered what happened to you.”

chapters.title: Her Father Calls After Five Years
chapters.desc: Six weeks of building a taxi called Nobody at night. Then a phone call from under the flyover, a photograph of her childhood camp bed with her husband’s face above it, and a note under his keys.
chapters.epigraph: “Gone to see my father. Don’t come.”

chapters.title: The Men Who Own Her Father
chapters.desc: Under the flyover a polite man in reading glasses swaps twelve stolen bikes for his dead brother’s two-stroke triple, running by seven. Her husband wanders in lost with dumplings, and finds a passage behind her father’s shelves.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m terribly sorry. I think I’m lost. Is this the right flyover?”

chapters.title: She Builds Her Way Out
chapters.desc: Three bores honed, nine rings freed, and a cracked crank seal that will seize the left cylinder at speed. “Lie to it.” Her father points at the wrong jet, Raiden kisses her for luck, and at 5:40 the widowmaker starts. Then Guo decides she’s too useful to let go.
chapters.epigraph: “Lie to it. Just this once. We’ll fix it properly after.”

chapters.title: He Stops Playing Dumb
chapters.desc: Guo breaks the deal and Dou draws a knife. Raiden steps in front of her, tells Dou where his mother lives and why he won’t use it, and tells Guo which beam in his building is cracked. She writes the settlement on a job card. At home his hands won’t stop shaking.
chapters.epigraph: “I know every building in this district. I know yours. You added two floors in 2019 on a frame drawn for four. Shall I tell you which beam?”

chapters.title: Her Father Says Sorry
chapters.desc: Her father sits on the black step and says sorry for the night she was seventeen. Raiden asks her before he raises the land. A pigeon loft on a river flat, a red door in daylight, and a no in Lin Jian’s kitchen. At New Year: thirty napkins, and “Ask me in March.”
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody has said no to me in my own kitchen since 1987. Sit down. Eat. You’re my daughter-in-law.”

chapters.title: She Lets Him In
chapters.desc: In the bath she tells him what happened at seventeen. She gives him the code to her cabinet, the day she left. The thirty-first napkin is two creepers under Carp, and on a Thursday at Mrs. Tong’s she puts on a steel ring she turned herself.
chapters.epigraph: “Oh-three-one-one. The day I left. It’s the code to everything I own that’s mine.”

chapters.title: The Masterpiece He Could Never Draw
chapters.desc: Jinx in a wig drives Nonna north while Serafina and Haozhen take Nobody the other way. Eighteen days. Two bullet holes in her taxi, a hug instead of a punch, and behind her own shutter she finally cries. He finishes her face.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t have to wait till you’re happy to draw your face.”

chapters.title: Her Name Over the Door
chapters.desc: He asks before he buys anything. She buys the chandler’s warehouse herself and he draws it for a dinner. Builders call her Boss, her father brings a pigeon named Jia, and a man in a good jacket wants a bike nobody can catch.
chapters.epigraph: “I named her Jia. Because she won’t go where she’s put.”

chapters.title: The Fire at the Shop
chapters.desc: A delivery rider’s battery goes at 2:09. Raiden runs barefoot and burns both palms on the shutter; she comes down the stair he insisted on, carrying a fuel tank. He sends the beam report to the city because people sleep above it, and tells Guo first.
chapters.epigraph: “You drew the stair, too.”

chapters.title: “Is That a Racetrack?”
chapters.desc: Serafina crashes at the Needle and Jinx spends two nights in a corridor she isn’t family enough to pass. Then a drawing on his desk: a house on a hill with a 1.2-kilometre driveway, and an option, not a purchase. A Saturday in the long grass.
chapters.epigraph: “Is that a racetrack?”

chapters.title: The Roof Never Falls
chapters.desc: A summer as her monkey on the driveway. The autumn hill climb on the old pass road with both fathers sharing a flask, and the class by 1.4 seconds. They move into Hill House in March, and on his birthday she says it first.
chapters.epigraph: “You’ve never said that first.”

chapters.title: Oil on His Cheek
chapters.desc: Six hours under Serafina’s gold bike, with her husband hovering and reading her the welder’s safety notice. She finds the bent selector fork, then draws a stripe of gearbox oil down his face.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ve been trying to get you to stop talking for six hours.”

chapters.title: She Tries to Cook
chapters.desc: The day after his birthday at the Walled City, where Ah Sim made two cakes for the first time, she tries his steamed fish. The oil catches. The extinguisher wins. The cake was behind the peaches.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s still mine. That’s what makes it mine.”

chapters.title: The Socialite Act at the Police Gala
chapters.desc: Sent to the police benevolent gala in his partner’s place, he plays the fool and mentions that the evidence store’s hinge pins are on the outside. An inspector sees through him. Jinx walks into a police building for the first time because she wants to.
chapters.epigraph: “Because nobody shoots the boy who can’t find his own coat.”

chapters.title: Locked in His Own Safe Room
chapters.desc: At the eighteen-month check on the Peak room he presses the button to test it, and it works. The owner’s code is on a plane and the house copy is in the house safe, inside. She brings the envelope in twenty-six minutes.
chapters.epigraph: “I knew who I’d ring. And I knew she’d come.”

chapters.title: The Golden Ratio Tattoo
chapters.desc: She’s never let anyone draw on her. At the end of August she asks him to: a spiral of gears below her collarbone with a pencil where the smallest gear goes. He cries at Dot’s. On the third night she’s done being an exhibit.
chapters.epigraph: “I never wanted anybody else’s drawing on me. This would be yours.”

chapters.title: He Names Her Bikes
chapters.desc: She gives him an engraving set and regrets it. GERALD on the dyno, MRS. TONG on a scooter, BOSS on a wheelbarrow, SHIPYARD ROAD under Carp’s tank. She cuts MONKEY herself, and NOT BAD LUCK for an apprentice, and MY HUSBAND.
chapters.epigraph: “Somebody gave me a chance once.”

extras.title: Architect
extras.line: He said it once, almost to himself. She remembered. Six weeks at the bench after closing.

extras.title: Four Visits
extras.line: The morning after the Peak drawings. His phone rang beside the peaches, and he never puts drawings away wrong.

descs.en: He blew open a shipping container expecting guns and found a princess. She won’t go home. She keeps coming back.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Lee Jun Hyuk goes to West Basin at midnight to kill the man who signs the papers. He blows the lock on the wrong container, expecting guns, and finds five women who have been in the dark for two days. One of them is standing between the door and the others with her hands open.

He gets them to a hospital and won’t give his name. Evangeline Lin finds him anyway. She’s the Lins’ quiet daughter, the paper twin, kept secret since she was three days old. He’s a big, kind, talkative man who hunts the people who move people, and he has a rule for everything.

She follows every rule but one. She keeps coming back.

Protector hero · He talks, she listens · Touch her and die · Complete in four volumes, plus ten side stories

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Evangeline says almost nothing in Thorns. I wanted to know what she’d say if someone waited long enough. The answer was: not much, and every word of it on purpose. So I gave her the man who talks more than anyone else in the series.

It’s a dark book in places. He has done terrible things for reasons he thinks are good, and the book doesn’t pretend otherwise. But mostly it’s about small things in dangerous rooms: towels folded in thirds, a lamp left on, a man practising a woman’s name in the shower.

He’s rich, by the way. He just never had anyone to spend it on.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers.

A dark romance with a lot of tenderness in it. It includes:

• Human trafficking, including a lorry where eleven women died

• Killings by the hero, on the page

• An infected knife wound and a high fever

• A dying man and morphine

• A photograph of a captive sold online

• An abduction attempt, a head injury and a shooting

• A man found dead in a refrigerated container

• A mother’s death in an aid station, remembered by her child

• Love scenes on the page

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
West Basin — The container terminal where it starts. Row K, the old control tower.
Nam's Noodles — Eleven tables on River Bridge Road in the border town. Phones go in a jar between the chilli oil and the soy sauce.
The karaoke flat — Two rooms over a karaoke bar that closed in 2019. Painted windows, three locks, a camp bed.
The menu — Nam's takeaway menu, taped inside the door, with his rules on the back (and two of hers).
The textile building — Eight storeys by the harbour. He owns it. Sixth floor: five windows of glass you can shoot at all day.
The window box — A steel greenhouse bolted to a twenty-centimetre ledge, behind a hatch cut into bulletproof glass.
The rabbit book — His school exercise book of names, boats and payments. There are ten in the end.
The Grey Lanterns — The border unit that took him in at eight. Old Ko's unit.
The court language — The language of the country she was born in, which is never named. She taught herself.
The heron — The gold crest on the blanket she was carried in: a heron over three peaks.
No. 9 Fig Tree Lane — The house with a real address. Thirty-one windows, and every one of them opens.
The Open Door — The foundation she starts for people who come out of boxes.
Rule seven — Don't come back.

chapters.title: The Container Had a Princess in It
chapters.desc: He went to West Basin to kill the man who signs the papers. On the way, he opens the wrong box.
chapters.epigraph: “If you want to live, stay behind me.”

chapters.title: Don’t Stop Moving
chapters.desc: She runs through the stacks holding a stranger’s hand while he talks the whole way. He goes up a tower for four minutes, and she counts every second of them.
chapters.epigraph: “If I’m not back in four minutes, you’re in charge. You look like you’re already in charge.”

chapters.title: He Leaves Her at a Hospital
chapters.desc: Harbourside General, three in the morning. He won’t give her his name, and he doesn’t look back. She keeps his jacket anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “I think I do.”

chapters.title: She Does Not Go Home
chapters.desc: Her father sends a car to the hospital, and for the first time in her life she sends it back. Then, before dawn, she asks Zhao Zhendong one question.
chapters.epigraph: “No.”

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept Showing Up
chapters.desc: Three days at a corner table in a noodle shop by the river bridge, two bowls every time. On the fourth day he comes in out of the rain and sits down at the cold one.
chapters.epigraph: “She orders two bowls. Every time. One for her and one that goes cold. I’ve stopped charging her for the cold one.”

chapters.title: He Does Not Own Towels
chapters.desc: He dries himself with yesterday’s T-shirt, so she brings him three white towels. On a Sunday she catches him folding them wrong, and he asks if he can kiss her.
chapters.epigraph: “You own something, you have to go back for it. Old Ko said that. Old Ko owned one spoon.”

chapters.title: Rules of a Safe House
chapters.desc: He comes home at three with another man’s blood on his cuff and finds the lamp still on. So he writes her seven rules on the back of a noodle menu, and she keeps six.
chapters.epigraph: “7. Don’t come back.”

chapters.title: She Watches the Exits
chapters.desc: Feet on the stair, and a back window he thought nobody knew about. She got there first. Then, in Nam’s back room, she tells him what she was raised to be.
chapters.epigraph: “Every house has a place where the sound carries. I’d found them all by the time I was seven.”

chapters.title: The Night He Had a Fever
chapters.desc: A knife wound sewn up in a village, six days of lying about it, and a fever of forty degrees. For once he can’t talk, so she does.
chapters.epigraph: “When people are scared, you keep talking, so they hear a voice that isn’t scared, and they follow the voice.”

chapters.title: Four Syllables
chapters.desc: Three weeks of healing, a spoon for a birthday that isn’t one, and a man practising four syllables in the shower.
chapters.epigraph: “That’s not a name. That’s a sentence.”

chapters.title: A Silver Ring With Coordinates Inside
chapters.desc: On her real birthday he puts a plain silver ring by her teacup. On Saturday a clerk by the bridge stamps the form, and at four in the morning she finds out why he was in a hurry.
chapters.epigraph: “If I don’t come back, this ring has the coordinates to a life where no one can find you. If I do come back, you’re mine.”

chapters.title: The Target Is a Judge
chapters.desc: He comes back over the river after thirteen days with honey and no Ferryman. In June he climbs seven flights to a judge who has left his door unlocked since March.
chapters.epigraph: “I wondered when you’d come. I’ve been leaving the door unlocked since March.”

chapters.title: She Asks Nothing
chapters.desc: In the dark her husband tells her about a barrier in the rain and waits for her to leave. Then the typhoon takes the power, and she lights the three candles from the drawer.
chapters.epigraph: “You opened mine.”

chapters.title: Her Sister Visits, Carrying Groceries
chapters.desc: Elowen comes up the border road with four bags of shopping and five of their mother’s lemons, and finally asks about the ring. Down on the bridge, her husband waits in a car.
chapters.epigraph: “I married a man who says one word. You found one who says all of them.”

chapters.title: She Wants a Window Box
chapters.desc: Strangers are asking about him at the border, so he moves them to a sixth floor with windows nobody can shoot through. They don’t open. She mentions basil once.
chapters.epigraph: “Basil would grow there.”

chapters.title: He Builds One Anyway
chapters.desc: A steel box six floors up, a hatch in the glass, and a pair of mended earrings. Then her sister’s wedding, which her husband attends from a roof across the street.
chapters.epigraph: “Good mend.”

chapters.title: The Traffickers Remember Her
chapters.desc: October is basil and a ridiculous pale blue coat. Then Eliana finds a photograph of Evangeline taken inside the box, and it is for sale.
chapters.epigraph: “Price on request. Serious buyers only. Palace interest welcome.”

chapters.title: He Goes Hunting
chapters.desc: A mahjong club above a car wash on Kiln Street, a man called Hwang, and four days. She keeps every rule he ever wrote, and doesn’t sleep.
chapters.epigraph: “If I’m not back by Sunday, go to your sister. Don’t wait up.” “I won’t.”

chapters.title: She Washes His Hands
chapters.desc: Warm water, a nail brush and ten fingers, one at a time. She doesn’t ask whose it was. When he wakes, he tells her about one reply, and the crest on it.
chapters.epigraph: “Why don’t you ask?” “Because you’d tell me.”

chapters.title: He Meets His Father-in-Law (Badly)
chapters.desc: A tracker in a birthday phone, a word on a scrap of paper in a locked drawer, and a knife held very still at her father’s throat. She is in the doorway when he says it.
chapters.epigraph: “Him.”

chapters.title: A Letter From a Palace
chapters.desc: He brings her father a kumquat tree for New Year. In March a letter comes from a palace, in a language she taught herself in a library.
chapters.epigraph: “I am sorry, my daughter.”

chapters.title: The Envoy at the Door
chapters.desc: A polite man in grey gloves, two guards on the step, and an offer with a husband already chosen. She asks him one question he won’t answer.
chapters.epigraph: “And who protects me from the people offering protection?”

chapters.title: She Says No to a Country
chapters.desc: On her real birthday she says no to a country in its own language. Then her husband has an afternoon, eleven telephone calls, and a viola.
chapters.epigraph: “You are my home.”

chapters.title: Two Men Share a Table
chapters.desc: Dinner for four at the house on the hill. Two sisters in the kitchen, two men on the terrace, and a payment for a boat in June.
chapters.epigraph: “If June is meant to be the month somebody comes to take me, I’d rather it was the month we made them sorry they tried.”

chapters.title: The Abduction Attempt
chapters.desc: Nam’s seventy-second birthday, which he refuses to have. A plan, a cake, and four men in a noodle shop at two in the afternoon.
chapters.epigraph: “Not again.”

chapters.title: She Shoots First
chapters.desc: Three shots in a noodle shop. The first two hit the duck. She is still very bad at it. It is enough.
chapters.epigraph: “Stay behind me.”

chapters.title: After
chapters.desc: Staples, a scan, a detective who knows exactly what her husband is, and a boat that won’t sail. That night she shakes until three, and he holds her the whole time.
chapters.epigraph: “I was choosing. I chose you.”

chapters.title: The Paper Twin
chapters.desc: Her brother comes to mend the air conditioning and draw the man who can’t lift anything, and tells her about eleven ribbons. Then her husband asks about a farm with a red gate.
chapters.epigraph: “I knew. I didn’t mind. You were ten.”

chapters.title: He Takes a Job He Hates
chapters.desc: He wants a real name, a payslip, and a job nobody comes through the door for. So he applies to the harbour board, opening containers at the Iron Docks.
chapters.epigraph: “Then let it be the job.”

chapters.title: The Throne Lets Her Go
chapters.desc: The twenty-first floor of the Harbour Hotel, a notary, a pen, and a man of forty-four with her eyes. He signs her free, and tells her her mother’s name.
chapters.epigraph: “Goodbye, little sister.”

chapters.title: A House With a Real Address
chapters.desc: A dark green door, windows that open, a glasshouse with nine pots in it, and a postbox with no name on it yet.
chapters.epigraph: “Hello, Mr. Lee.”

chapters.title: The Neighbours Bring a Cake
chapters.desc: A neighbour brings a chestnut cake and he checks it. A ginger cat moves in. Then her father carries a cedar chest up four stone steps on his own.
chapters.epigraph: “Because you came back.”

chapters.title: He Doesn’t Know How to Sleep Without a Weapon
chapters.desc: He doesn’t know how to sleep in a house with no gun under the bed. So she sleeps on his side, between him and the door.
chapters.epigraph: “Nowhere. That’s the point.”

chapters.title: The Last Target
chapters.desc: Nam rings on a Thursday night. The Ferryman is back on the river after nine years, with thirty people and a date. Jun Hyuk takes the rifle out, and his wife sits down opposite him.
chapters.epigraph: “Let me show you you’re allowed forgiveness.”

chapters.title: She Asks Him Not to Go
chapters.desc: She has asked him questions, and asked him to teach her, and asked him to come home. She has never once asked him to stay. Tonight she runs down the lane barefoot.
chapters.epigraph: “Then let me be the first.”

chapters.title: He Goes Anyway — Then Turns Back
chapters.desc: The bank above the old jetty, eleven at night, a rifle, and a bag of exercise books. At 12:41 he rings his wife.
chapters.epigraph: “I can’t hear anything but you.”

chapters.title: Staying
chapters.desc: Ten exercise books through a car window at midnight, a rifle handed over a desk, and a lamp on three extension leads at the gate.
chapters.epigraph: “I want to learn how to stay.”

chapters.title: Someone Else Finishes It
chapters.desc: Friday the thirteenth of December, before dawn, a farmhouse on the far side of the river. He hears about it on the inspection-shed television.
chapters.epigraph: “Tell the truth when they ask you. And remember them.”

chapters.title: A Wedding With Six Guests
chapters.desc: The longest night of the year, a garden in December, herbs from the glasshouse, and a groom who can only say one word.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ll keep choosing her.”

chapters.title: Forgiven
chapters.desc: Epilogue. Three years later, the longest night again. Eleven rosemary bushes taller than the wall, and a letter with no name on it.
chapters.epigraph: “You do not owe anybody anything any more.”

chapters.title: A Princess at the Supermarket
chapters.desc: November 2022. She is twenty-four and has never once bought her own groceries. He follows her round the supermarket at six metres.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to know everything the first time.”

chapters.title: He Tries to Cook Breakfast
chapters.desc: November 2024, Fig Tree Lane. He wants to bring her breakfast in bed, once, like a man in a video. Mrs. Bae brings an extinguisher from 1987.
chapters.epigraph: “Love has made you both strange.”

chapters.title: The Neighbour’s Cat Chose Him
chapters.desc: Winter 2024. A ginger cat with half an ear, a terrible thief, decides the big man next door belongs to him.
chapters.epigraph: “Move, Sergeant.”

chapters.title: She Learns to Shoot
chapters.desc: February 2024, a range in an orchard in the hills. She misses fourteen times and hits the compost heap once.
chapters.epigraph: “Three is a room.”

chapters.title: He Learns Her Favourite Colour
chapters.desc: October 2023, a year to the day after West Basin. He has bought her blue things for a year. Nobody ever asked.
chapters.epigraph: “It isn’t really the colour. It’s that it reminds me doors can open.”

chapters.title: The Borderland Boy
chapters.desc: Spring 1999. A boy of eight with a name written inside his collar, an aid station on the river road, and a sergeant with one spoon.
chapters.epigraph: “That’s a big name for a small boy.”

chapters.title: Paper Twins
chapters.desc: April 2025. For seventeen years Raiden has said he’s the older twin. Then the King sends her birth entry.
chapters.epigraph: “You made me a day.”

chapters.title: He Talks for Both of Them
chapters.desc: The Chen Foundation’s spring gala, May 2025, as Aurelia sees it. Her husband talks to everyone so she never has to.
chapters.epigraph: “She turned down a husband. The crown came with him.”

chapters.title: The Silver Ring Engraving
chapters.desc: Spring 2026. Two lines of numbers inside a silver ring, worn for three years. A house across the river that she has never seen.
chapters.epigraph: “So you’re her. I’ve had the sheets aired every Thursday for three years.”

chapters.title: Clean Towels
chapters.desc: October 2025. She goes to the lake country for four days to play her mother’s air. He folds twenty-two towels.
chapters.epigraph: “One for you to fix.”

extras.title: Paper Birthday
extras.line: The date on his papers is wrong. She writes it down anyway, and goes looking for a spoon.

extras.title: Every Word
extras.line: Thirteen days over the river. She hardly speaks. He finds out where she keeps the rest.

descs.en: She saw through the guard nobody else noticed. He has spent ten years making people disappear, and now he wants to disappear with her.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
At a government reception on Battery Hill, sixty guards watch the guests. One of them watches a single man for forty-one minutes, and the only person who notices is Serafina Song, there on a staff pass to inspect a red rally car, in her sister’s dress and her own boots.

She walks across the ballroom and tells him he isn’t a guard. She’s right. Qin Haozhen has spent ten years making people disappear for a state that doesn’t put its name on doors, and nobody has ever looked at him before.

She asks him for a race, not a date. A man who sleeps four hours a night in any bed in any country falls asleep in her passenger seat at three in the morning, and keeps coming back.

Spy and racing driver · She sees him first · Morally grey hero · Complete in four volumes, plus side stories

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
In Terms, Serafina turned up at her sister’s wedding in Milan after two years’ silence, with oil on her boots, and drove the bride away from her own reception. I always wanted to know who could keep up with her.

The answer was the most forgettable man in the room. Haozhen isn’t a good man when this book begins, and it doesn’t pretend he is. It’s about a man finding out he’s allowed to want something, starting with an egg sandwich, and a woman who decides every morning whether she can live with the truth about him.

The racing is as real as I could make it. The spy work stays at story level. And yes, the car really can do two hundred miles an hour. He did the brakes.

characters.title: Characters

chars.name: Serafina Song
chars.role: Female Lead · racing driver and mechanic, Team AURELIA
chars.appearance: Tall and thin, short dark hair she cuts herself with kitchen scissors, an old burn on the back of her right hand, oil to the elbows. Leather jacket, black jeans, boots worn down on the outside the way a driver’s heels wear.
chars.personality:
Loud, quick and very funny
Swears in three languages — Italian, English and the city’s own
Names every car she owns
Taps a fingernail on her front teeth when she’s working something out
Eats standing up
chars.strengths:
Brakes on the marker, to the metre
Sees the gap a second before anyone else
Decides every day, and means it
chars.weaknesses:
Goes for gaps that are too small
Hates being paid for
Won’t eat fish (and does, once, for a reason)
chars.nickname: Sera · the gilded bird’s sister · ‘Rich girl’ (Granny Shum)
chars.favHabit: Driving the long loop at three in the morning: bridge, tunnel, coast road

chars.name: Qin Haozhen (秦浩真 · Qín Hàozhēn)
chars.appearance: Medium height, medium build, a forgettable dark suit and a face that slides out of your memory. A small notch at the end of his left eyebrow. Very clean hands. Later: a long pale line down his left forearm, stitched with fishing line.
chars.personality:
A man of few words, all of them in complete sentences
Dry humour he never announces
Checks the perimeter before breakfast
Takes his watch off and lays it face down when something matters
Keeps lists; colour-codes spreadsheets
chars.strengths:
Notices everything, a week before anyone tells him

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers.

A fast, funny book, with some hard moments:

• A state operative’s work, including abductions and killings, mostly remembered

• A man taken from his family in front of his young son

• Trauma, depression and silence after a mission

• A cruel parent and a family’s money troubles

• Threats and surveillance

• A car chase, gunfire and a gunshot wound, stitched without a doctor

• A serious racing crash and a long recovery

• Illegal street racing

• Love scenes on the page

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Nonna — Serafina’s red 1992 Italian rally hatchback, named after their grandmother.
Gilded — Team AURELIA’s matte black race car, number 7, with AURELIA in gold on the bonnet.
Nobody — The getaway car: a grey 2006 estate with wooden-bead seat covers and an engine it should never have had.
Two Hundred — A burnt-out 1991 endurance prototype, bought for scrap.
The garage — Under the railway bridge in the industrial district. Trains every eleven minutes.
Granny Shum’s — The Saturday street races by the paint works: the long straight, the S-bends, the lamp posts round the gas works.
The Needle — The hairpin at the end of the back straight at the circuit in the north.
The Eleventh — The Bureau Haozhen worked for, in a building with no name on it.
Brake on the marker — Braking exactly at the board, to the metre.
Telemetry — The car’s data: speed, throttle, brake and steering, a thousand times a second.

chapters.title: The Guard Nobody Else Noticed
chapters.desc: Serafina is on Battery Hill to check a car for a forged plate, and she spots a guard who isn’t guarding anyone. So she walks over and tells him.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re the only one looking at the right person.”

chapters.title: She Finds Out His Name
chapters.desc: Three weeks, one bribed caterer and a note about his terrible brakes. Then the guard turns up in her garage in the middle of the night to ask her to stop.
chapters.epigraph: “A car tells you everything about the man who drives it. His just told me to mind my own business.”

chapters.title: A Race, Not a Date
chapters.desc: She makes him race her at Granny Shum’s, his grey taxi of a car against her red rally hatchback. He loses on purpose, and she’s furious about it.
chapters.epigraph: “A circuit is a circuit and a road is a road, and I’m not giving up the road for anybody.”

chapters.title: Rematch
chapters.desc: A track day in the north, one car, two drivers and Mouse on the stopwatch. This time he drives like himself, and she kisses him in the empty paddock.
chapters.epigraph: “Five laps each, same car, Mouse on the clock. Then we both know.”

chapters.title: 3 A.M., Passenger Seat
chapters.desc: He hasn’t slept properly in ten years. Then he falls asleep in her passenger seat, and she drives round the harbour till dawn so he won’t wake up.
chapters.epigraph: “In ten years I’ve never sat in a car I wasn’t driving or guarding.”

chapters.title: What He Does for Work
chapters.desc: Mouse finds the missing Belgian in a newspaper and a camera in the garage roof. Serafina lays out everything she knows on the workbench, and he doesn’t tell her she’s wrong.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t lie to you. I’ve never lied to you. I just haven’t told you most of it.”

chapters.title: She Should Run
chapters.desc: She knows exactly how to run. Instead she turns up outside his flat at six in the morning with two egg sandwiches and four rules.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to run. I’m the one people run with.”

chapters.title: The First Time He Bleeds in Her Garage
chapters.desc: He’s late for Valentine’s dinner because of a knife in a stairwell. He comes in bleeding with cold dumplings, and won’t go near the Bureau doctor.
chapters.epigraph: “Rule two doesn’t cover blood. Sit down before you fall on my car.”

chapters.title: Twelve Days and a Postcard
chapters.desc: He’s gone for twelve days with no phone. She nearly puts Gilded into the tyre wall, Aurelia notices, and then a postcard comes with nothing written on it.
chapters.epigraph: “When you can tell me, tell me. That’s how it works in my house.”

chapters.title: The Ring Was in the Glovebox
chapters.desc: She goes into his glovebox for the tyre gauge and finds a ring. He had a speech in four parts, and she says yes before he gets to part two.
chapters.epigraph: “I had a plan. It had four parts. You were supposed to let me finish.”

chapters.title: He Has Never Planned a Party
chapters.desc: He has stood at the door of eleven weddings and never been inside one, so he makes a list. Then he puts the engagement on a Bureau form, she buys a burnt-out race car, and he forgets his own toast.
chapters.epigraph: “Depends how many people love you. Start counting.”

chapters.title: Her Sister Finds Out Who Pays for the Racing Team
chapters.desc: Aurelia does the team’s books and finds sixty thousand she didn’t pay. At Da Gianni the whole restaurant hears whose salary bought Sera’s gearbox.
chapters.epigraph: “He overpaid by a third. I like him.”

chapters.title: Two Professionals at One Table
chapters.desc: Dinner on the forty-fourth floor. Two men go for the same chair, the ruby moves to the right finger, and Chen Si takes Haozhen out on the balcony.
chapters.epigraph: “Mr. Qin. Welcome. You don’t exist.”

chapters.title: Director Duan Sends Congratulations
chapters.desc: His director has read the form. She brings congratulations, a silver pen with a 7 on it, and a folder for Lisbon. Serafina uses the pen to enter a hill climb.
chapters.epigraph: “We look after our families. It’s in the training.”

chapters.title: Five A.M., Departures
chapters.desc: The last night before Lisbon, then the airport at five in the morning. She gives him her grandmother’s tyre gauge, and he says it through the car window.
chapters.epigraph: “You have to bring it back. It’s the only one that reads true. I’ll need it for the hill climb.”

chapters.title: Baizhang Pass
chapters.desc: She races up a mountain without her gauge. On the other side of the world, a man and a night porter watch the stream at four in the morning.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s a waste of good tyres. His tyres.”

chapters.title: The Target Has a Family
chapters.desc: Lisbon. Twenty-three days in a chair by a door, counting a boy’s keepy-ups. Then the job.
chapters.epigraph: “Not in front of the house. Please. That’s my son’s window.”

chapters.title: He Comes Home Wrong
chapters.desc: He comes home, sits in her passenger seat and says nothing for two days. Her father’s company is falling apart, and in the end he tells her about the boy.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to ask. I’m going to sit here. You talk when there’s something you can say.”

chapters.title: Her Family Opposes the Match
chapters.desc: Her mother writes for the first time in seven years: bring him. The house on the Peak has lot numbers on everything, and her mother asks him nine questions.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody keeps her, madam. I’d like to be wherever she is. That’s all I’m asking for.”

chapters.title: A Getaway Car Nobody Knows
chapters.desc: Rule four, at the kettle: he wants out. That means a car nobody knows, so they go to Jinx.
chapters.epigraph: “One order. No questions. And you never bring it back here with a hole in it.”

chapters.title: The Mission He Didn’t Take
chapters.desc: A grey building in the capital that isn’t on any map. A seventh-floor office with a radiator that knocks. A thin folder about a journalist in Singapore. For the first time in eleven years, he says one word to the state.
chapters.epigraph: “Do you know what happens to people who say no, Haozhen?” “Yes, Director. I’ve driven them.”

chapters.title: A File on the Workbench
chapters.desc: A Saturday afternoon. He’s in the north for his mother’s birthday. A woman of fifty-five in a grey coat ducks under the shutter with a shopping bag and her knitting, asks very politely for hot water, and sits on his stool. When she leaves, there’s a file on the bench. Forty photographs. One of them was taken that morning.
chapters.epigraph: “I thought I was watching out for her.”

chapters.title: Leverage
chapters.desc: Eleven years of black notebooks in his own code, hidden under a laundry cat’s heated bed. One line in a stolen ledger: two initials and the word “Private”. A month of nights at the workbench, Mouse at the end of it finding companies, and three copies of a file nobody in the capital knows exists.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re starting to exist.”

chapters.title: The Resignation Letter That Took Ten Years
chapters.desc: The New Year comes and goes and nobody calls. Lunar New Year comes and goes. So he goes to them, uninvited, on a Monday in February, with one sentence on a page torn from his notebook and the first page of an index. A quiet office, a radiator that knocks, and a woman who doesn’t stop knitting until she reads the word Northgate.
chapters.epigraph: “I resign. — Qin Haozhen.”

chapters.title: They Send Someone
chapters.desc: The season opener at the circuit in the north. Eleven thousand people in the grandstand, a black car with a gold name, and in the pit lane, with a hospitality lanyard and a stick of cinnamon gum, the boy from the next bed in a dormitory of forty, who once gave his window seat to nobody but him.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re already here.”

chapters.title: Shoot the Tyres
chapters.desc: A closed service station on the old coast road, a car wash, and a grey taxi with the engine already running. Three cars behind them, then two, then one. She drives. He shoots out tyres. Nobody dies who didn’t have to, and one man who nearly does is pulled out of the fire by the friend he was sent to bring in.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not asking you to be brave. I’m asking you to stay awake.”

chapters.title: The Safe House in the Mountains
chapters.desc: A stone house above the tea terraces at Yunwu, a dead man’s photograph on the shrine, two deaf neighbours who bring eggs and ask nothing, a stray dog that stops dead in front of you, and rain on a tin roof. A fever, and then fourteen days with nowhere to be. The best two weeks of their lives.
chapters.epigraph: “The garage. Under the bridge.”

chapters.title: A Truce in the Tea Terraces
chapters.desc: A black car in the tea terraces. A minister who has tea with Aurelia on the first Thursday of every month. A month of waiting, and then a quiet room in the old town where everything he ever wrote down goes into a stove. Two prices. He pays them both without asking. That night, at last, she asks him for the number, and he tells her.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to tell you it was fine.”

chapters.title: Disavowed
chapters.desc: Nine quiet months: a championship, a prize in Geneva, a man learning to sleep six hours and cook. Then a registered letter from the capital informs him that no person called Qin Haozhen has ever existed, and asks him to sign to confirm he received it. For the first time in years, he laughs until he can’t stand up. And with it comes a parcel, two metres long, in red wool.
chapters.epigraph: “For the first who walked out.”

chapters.title: A Man With No File
chapters.desc: A mining town that the maps stopped bothering with, a registry clerk who remembers a boy on the wall by the winding gear, and his mother at her Japanese sewing machine, who has never once believed he was a security guard. Then a driving test he fails for checking his mirrors too often. And Harbour Road, on a Friday afternoon, holding her hand where anyone can see.
chapters.epigraph: “Now I exist.”

chapters.title: Her Family Was Not Invited
chapters.desc: Now that he exists, Mr. Kwok says, there has to be a proper engagement dinner. Six dishes, trestle tables, borrowed chairs, two mothers who have never met, and the trains every eleven minutes. Her parents were not invited. At eight o’clock, they come in under the shutter anyway, and her mother is carrying a folder.
chapters.epigraph: “To the top.”

chapters.title: Last Race in the Industrial District
chapters.desc: A works team from Modena wants her for the rest of the season and all of next. Page nine of the contract says she gives up the road. So she goes back to Granny Shum’s for one last Saturday, against a kid in a purple coupé who was filming from a car roof the night she met the taxi, and a woman from Modena is standing in the crowd.
chapters.epigraph: “You’ve carried enough things that weren’t yours. Now you carry her home.”

chapters.title: Overqualified
chapters.desc: Orsini Corse needs a head of security for its Asian operation. His CV is one line long and says “References: none available.” Donatella Ferri asks why she should hire him. He tells her eleven things wrong with her paddock that he noticed on the walk from the car park. Then the twelfth.
chapters.epigraph: “Only a small one.”

chapters.title: Pit Wall
chapters.desc: Speed traces, brake pressure, throttle, steering angle: four coloured lines on a screen, a thousand times a second. He learns to read them the way he used to read rooms. He finds something in her data nobody else has seen. And at the end of the pit wall, after three years, Mouse finally says a word to him.
chapters.epigraph: “That was good.”

chapters.title: The Needle
chapters.desc: The home round. Her parents in the grandstand for the first time. Lap thirty-one, the end of the back straight, a backmarker’s engine letting go a few seconds before she arrives. He sees it in the data before anyone sees it on the screens: brake pressure at maximum, and the speed not coming down.
chapters.epigraph: “Together.”

chapters.title: Hospital, Night Two
chapters.desc: The ninth floor of the big hospital on the hill. A collarbone, three ribs, a bruised lung, a brain that has been shaken very hard. A machine breathing for her. “Family only,” says the nurse. Her mother says something nobody expected. Thirty hours later, at two in the morning, she opens her eyes and asks about the car.
chapters.epigraph: “Car?”

chapters.title: She Drives Again
chapters.desc: Four months. A plate in her collarbone, headaches that come like weather, a red arm sling with a mountain road on it, and a simulator where she freezes at the Needle every time. Then a January morning at the circuit in the north. He doesn’t stop her. He holds her helmet.
chapters.epigraph: “I won’t stop you. And I won’t push you.”

chapters.title: Just Married at Three Hundred and Twenty-Two
chapters.desc: A registry office at ten past nine, where he finally gets a piece of paper that says what he is to her. Nine dishes in a garage under a railway bridge, and the middle of a wedding, at last, from the inside. Then rice, and a grey taxi, and the old military airstrip at sunset, where something red is waiting under a tarpaulin with his handwriting on its nose.
chapters.epigraph: “I get to go home with you.”

chapters.title: First Podium
chapters.desc: A whole season without one. Fourth, fifth, fourth, sixth. Then the finale at the circuit in the north, a year and a month after the Needle, with two mothers and Granny Shum in Stand B and a red works car in her mirrors on the last lap. Third place. Champagne in his face. He lets it happen.
chapters.epigraph: “Come home. I’ll be here.”

chapters.title: A Garage With Two Names on the Door
chapters.desc: Epilogue. Two years on. The garage under the railway bridge has a sign at last. There’s a team, and a junior driver who used to film from a car roof, and three postcards on the whiteboard. One of them has a football drawn on it, and a number. And at three in the morning, someone different is driving the loop.
chapters.epigraph: “My road.” “Our road.”

chapters.title: He Learns to Lose at Karaoke
chapters.desc: December 2023. The team Christmas, in a karaoke room above Mr. Kwok’s favourite bar. Big Wu scores forty-one. Mr. Kwok sings for his late wife. And a man who has spent eleven years being forgettable tries very hard to sing badly, and she catches him lifting at the gas works.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re allowed to be bad at something, Hao.”

chapters.title: She Teaches Him to Change a Tyre
chapters.desc: December 2022, the week after the track day. She decides that any man who sits in her passenger seat should be able to change a wheel. He says he’s never done it. She times him: fourteen minutes. Then, one wet night in the alley, she sees him do it in ninety seconds.
chapters.epigraph: “It was how quietly he could arrange to be taught.”

chapters.title: The Security Guard Who Smiled Once
chapters.desc: August 2025, the Orsini paddock, as told by Callum Hart. There is a pool. Forty-one people have put money on who can make the head of security smile first. Callum tries jokes, a video of a goat, and an Italian mechanic in a wig. Witnesses are still recovering.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody was paying her.”

chapters.title: Who Is Faster: the Car or the Bike?
chapters.desc: August 2024. An argument at Lunar New Year that has been going on for six months. A track day, the main straight at the circuit in the north, a matte black car and a motorbike Jinx built from nothing. Everybody has a bet. Raiden is holding the money, which is the first mistake.
chapters.epigraph: “You won, Sera.”

chapters.title: He Checks the Perimeter Before Breakfast
chapters.desc: Spring 2027. Every morning, before the egg sandwiches, he walks the garage: shutter, side door, alley, loft window, the roof hatch, the stairs. Every morning. She starts timing it. Four minutes and twelve seconds on day one. She keeps a chart on the whiteboard for a month. Then one morning he forgets.
chapters.epigraph: “I just don’t need to go and look.”

chapters.title: The Military Academy at Sixteen
chapters.desc: September 2010. A slow train south from a mining town, a dormitory of forty boys under a roof that leaks onto bed eleven, a firing range in the snow, and a boy who laughs with his whole face and gives away the window seat. Two years later, a woman with red wool on her needles asks a question about a map. The boy they chose because he never hesitated.
chapters.epigraph: “You can’t spend your whole life waiting for somebody to tell you where to go.”

chapters.title: Forty-Three Songs for the Car
chapters.desc: Nonna’s tape deck has been broken since 2017 and Serafina plays everything off her phone, in the same order, every time: forty-three songs, and she always skips the seventeenth. He doesn’t own a single piece of music. Over a summer he learns all forty-three, by heart, in order. Then he fixes the tape deck.
chapters.epigraph: “Because you always come home.”

chapters.title: Wedding Planning With a Spreadsheet
chapters.desc: February 2026. Two hundred guests, nine round tables, one garage, and a laptop open on the long table on the forty-fourth floor. He has colour-coded everyone. There is a column for who must face the door. There is a column called “Score-neutral”. Aurelia reads it for an hour without speaking, and then says the nicest thing she has ever said to anyone who wasn’t her husband.
chapters.epigraph: “I want you to be able to find me.”

chapters.title: The Youngest Sister Hacks the Bodyguard
chapters.desc: March 2025. Zhao is in Rotterdam and the youngest Lin sister is giving a talk about a bank that would rather she didn’t. Elowen asks for a favour. He has no identity card, no job and a brand-new phone. She has his phone open in four minutes. He is very impressed. She is very annoyed that he is impressed.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t make it weird.”

chapters.title: The Fake Name He Liked Best
chapters.desc: May 2027, a ferry on Lake Como, on the way to see an old man with eleven cars and a parrot and a red rally car with a forged chassis plate. He has had nineteen names. On the ferry, he tells her about the one he liked best: a deckhand called Ah Sang, on an island boat in a southern sea, whom nobody ever wanted anything from. She calls him by it once.
chapters.epigraph: “I want you to use mine.”

extras.title: Little Finger
extras.line: Twelve days with no phone, a crack in the splitter, a blank postcard from Monza, and something in the glovebox behind the tissues.

extras.title: Car?
extras.line: The night she comes home from the ninth floor. His phone is charging beside the mug. Where was he while she wasn’t anywhere?

descs.en: She proposed with eleven pages of terms. Clause nine is about the bedroom. Clause ten is a single word.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
On her father’s birthday, in front of two hundred guests, Aurelia Song’s mother raises a glass and announces that her daughter’s jewellery boutique is losing four million a year and will close in January. Aurelia walks out onto the balcony in gold silk, shaking, doing sums in her head. A stranger gives her his coat.

Three days later he walks into her boutique and asks to rent it. His name is Chen Si. He runs the Syndicate. She names a price instead: a seat at his table.

Then she proposes. Eleven pages, in red ink. Clause nine is about the bedroom. Clause ten is a single word.

Contract marriage · Power couple · He never asks her to win · Complete in four volumes, plus side stories

21+ · For adult readers.

Glamorous and sharp, with some dark moments:

• A mother who humiliates her daughter in public

• Organised crime, threats and a car attack

• A poisoning and a long recovery from intensive care

• A panic attack, and therapy

• A father’s wrongful arrest and death in custody, and a riot in a youth detention centre, remembered

• Power play between a married couple: a contract, blindfolds, silk ties and a safe word

• Love scenes on the page

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Aurelia was the rival in Thorns: gold, sunglasses, a slap in the rain, a running score. I wanted to know who she was at two in the morning, when nobody was watching her walk. This is her book.

The crime stays at story level. The jewellery is as real as I could make it: piercing saws, gravers, links soldered one at a time, rouge on the wheel for the last pass.

Second is just the first of the ones who kept going.

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
AURELIA — Aurelia’s jewellery boutique on Harbour Road.
The Syndicate — The organisation Chen Si runs. Thirty years old, and older than him.
The terms — Aurelia’s price for laundering money through her shop: a share, real pieces, the books, no lies, a seat at the table.
The marriage agreement — Eleven clauses, renewable after ten years, when the Wife may rewrite every one. At the renewal, he adds a twelfth and a thirteenth.
Clause twelve — The Wife is not the Husband’s queen.
The word — The safe word written into the agreement. It is “Milan.”
Numero Uno — The necklace she named at two in the morning, after a phone call with her mother.
The Jade Hall — A restaurant on Temple Street with a round table for twelve. It has belonged to the Syndicate for thirty years.
The house on the Peak — Her parents’ house, where the party for her father’s fifty-seventh birthday was held.
The Song Group — Her father’s company.
The Pearl — The restaurant booked for New Year’s Eve, same as always.
Tesoro — Her father’s name for her, from before Vienna.

chapters.title: The Balcony Where He Lent Her His Coat
chapters.desc: Her mother closes her shop in the middle of a birthday toast. Out on the balcony, a stranger lends her his coat and doesn’t try to make it better.
chapters.epigraph: “The world is obsessed with your shine. I’m more interested in what you do in the dark.”

chapters.title: The Man Who Wanted to Rent Her Shop
chapters.desc: He comes to her shop offering to wash his money through it. She crosses out his terms in red ink and names her own price.
chapters.epigraph: “You want my shop. I want a seat at your table. Those are the terms.”

chapters.title: She Negotiates a Don Into a Corner
chapters.desc: She takes him to a basement with no menu and finds a thief in his books before the fish goes cold. Under a streetlamp, he stops waiting.
chapters.epigraph: “I only drink what I take.”

chapters.title: She Does Not Do Second Place
chapters.desc: He takes away the chairs to see what she will do, so she sits in his. Then she kisses him in it and wins every hand of mahjong in the building.
chapters.epigraph: “Rule one of a room full of men who want you gone: sit down first.”

chapters.title: The First Ledger She Ever Read
chapters.desc: Her first crate gets through customs at dawn, and she loves every minute. That night at her counter he looks at her mouth, and leaves.
chapters.epigraph: “It isn’t that I like breaking rules. I like knowing exactly which ones I’m breaking, and what they cost.”

chapters.title: He Never Asks Her to Win
chapters.desc: She loses a game of chess on purpose to see what he’ll do. He lays down his own king.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t care if you win, Aurelia. I don’t care if you lose. You could lose every game you ever play me and I’d just want another one.”

chapters.title: Dinner on the Forty-Fourth Floor
chapters.desc: He cooks her dinner and tells her how his parents died. Then she tells him to kneel, and he does.
chapters.epigraph: “Take off your watch. I don’t want you counting.”

chapters.title: A Proposal With Terms and Conditions
chapters.desc: She proposes with eleven pages of red ink. He signs every one, and writes something in the margin she can’t argue with.
chapters.epigraph: “Not everything has to be perfect to be worth keeping.”

chapters.title: Her Parents Are Not Told
chapters.desc: She marries him in Milan with eleven guests and the sister she hasn’t spoken to in two years, and her mother finds out from a magazine.
chapters.epigraph: “Shouldn’t we tell your parents?” “We will. They read Gilt.”

chapters.title: Blood Brothers at the Reception
chapters.desc: Zhao makes a nine-word speech and Serafina offers her a getaway car. On the wedding night, the bride blindfolds her husband with her veil.
chapters.epigraph: “He is my brother. You’re his. So you’re family.”

chapters.title: A Necklace on the Hit List
chapters.desc: She finishes the best necklace she’s ever made and lays it over her husband’s shoulders while he stares at his list. Then she makes him count the stones out loud.
chapters.epigraph: “Forty-one sapphires. Not one of them bought by Chen Si.”

chapters.title: He Lost an Argument (Once)
chapters.desc: A grey car follows her, and he wants two men behind her everywhere. She wins the argument with a cancelled shipment, three days at Zhao’s range and a page of red ink.
chapters.epigraph: “He lost. Good.”

chapters.title: Her Family Is Coming to Dinner
chapters.desc: Her mother writes to invite herself to dinner. Chen Si cooks the fish, Aurelia leaves the dishwasher whining on purpose, and at the door her mother names the one man he can’t stand.
chapters.epigraph: “We would like to be proud of you.”

chapters.title: What Her Father Wants
chapters.desc: Over risotto at Da Gianni, her father asks Chen Si to write to Fu Jianguo. Then he admits he’s already told Fu no.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s only a letter. A few lines. Your name at the bottom. It would mean so much.”

chapters.title: She Says No to Her Mother
chapters.desc: She tells her mother no in front of the maids. Then she and Mr. Lu work out how to get at Fu through his son.
chapters.epigraph: “No, Mamma. Not for the bridge. Not for you. Not ever.”

chapters.title: Her Mother’s Last Card
chapters.desc: Her mother sends a photograph of Serafina at a street race and names her price. Aurelia keeps it from Chen Si for one night and goes to the garage under the railway bridge.
chapters.epigraph: “You have something I want, tesoro. And I have your sister.”

chapters.title: The Racing Team She Pretends Not to Fund
chapters.desc: Aurelia sells Fu Kang a watch from Geneva and follows his money all the way to his father’s name. She also learns to change a wheel and rebuilds her sister’s sponsorship deck in one night.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t pretend to fund it any more.” “No. Now I pretend I’m not terrified.”

chapters.title: Sisters at a Racetrack
chapters.desc: Serafina wins the last race of the season with AURELIA on her bonnet. Chen Si goes up to the VIP lounge to have a word with her mother.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t watch the car. Watch the gap. The car goes where the gap is.”

chapters.title: My Queen Is Not a Title
chapters.desc: Aurelia wears a dress of gold to her mother’s Christmas party, and Chen Si calls her his queen in front of Fu Jianguo. Upstairs, in her old room, he makes her watch herself in the mirror.
chapters.epigraph: “She doesn’t need my name. She has her own.”

chapters.title: A Snake in the Syndicate
chapters.desc: Someone parks a lorry across the coast road in front of Zhao’s car. Chen Si comes home with shaking hands, knowing Sun Wei sold his diary, and decides to go to Sun Wei’s New Year’s Eve dinner anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “Zhendong doesn’t brake.”

chapters.title: The Glass of Wine at the Harbour Dinner
chapters.desc: New Year’s Eve on a boat called the Pearl. She chooses the wine. She opens every bottle herself. At midnight he takes her glass, because he only drinks what he takes. Twenty minutes later, his hand starts to shake.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ll come home with you.”

chapters.title: The Week He Couldn’t Get Out of Bed
chapters.desc: A private room on the ninth floor with no name on the door. A heart that won’t keep time. A rumour, by the second of January, that the Don is dying. And a woman in yesterday’s gold, running everything in his name.
chapters.epigraph: “Somebody has to.”

chapters.title: She Signs His Name
chapters.desc: Forty documents in three days. One forged signature, perfect. A transfer Sun Wei tries to slip through at midnight. And Enzo, at three in the morning, teaching her the last stroke.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t make me use my wife’s privileges.”

chapters.title: The Board Meeting Without a Don
chapters.desc: A private room in the old town, twelve men, one empty chair at the head of the table. Sun Wei has prepared a speech about continuity. Aurelia walks in alone, in black, and sits down before he can give it.
chapters.epigraph: “And nobody mistakes my patience for not knowing.”

chapters.title: The Traitor at the Table
chapters.desc: She invites the senior men to dinner on the forty-fourth floor. Eleven guests, a soup that takes eight hours, and a list of three names in her head before anyone picks up a spoon.
chapters.epigraph: “She never made enough for just one person.”

chapters.title: What She Does to the Traitor
chapters.desc: Not a gun. Not a knife. Not Zhao. Contracts, deeds, a frozen account, a forty-page file, and one suitcase. Quietly. Thoroughly. Completely. By breakfast, Sun Wei owns nothing but the clothes he is standing in.
chapters.epigraph: “You didn’t need a gun.”

chapters.title: His Brother Guards the Door
chapters.desc: Fourteen nights on a plastic chair outside a room on the ninth floor. A woman with a syringe. A woman who falls asleep on his shoulder at four in the morning. Zhao Zhendong has never had a sister. He finds out what it is like.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re a good brother.”

chapters.title: A Laptop, a Gun, and a Very Tired Co-Ruler
chapters.desc: His first night home. He wakes at three in the morning and she is in the chair beside the bed, asleep sitting up, with a laptop on her knees and a gun on the table and his necklace at her throat. He finally understands what he married.
chapters.epigraph: “Just you, in this bed, not dying.”

chapters.title: He Is Weak for Six Weeks
chapters.desc: No stairs. No work. No anger. No sex. He hates every minute. She makes him eat. And on the forty-second day, when Dr. Ma finally says yes, the Wife reads clause nine very carefully, and finds a way to make sure he doesn’t lift a finger.
chapters.epigraph: “I didn’t marry your strength, Chen Si. I married you.”

chapters.title: The Word Is Milan
chapters.desc: The danger is over. He is safe. She is fine. She is fine for nine days. On the tenth, in the middle of the boutique, holding a champagne flute for a client, her hands stop working. She says the word for the first time, and it isn’t in bed.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to earn being frightened.”

chapters.title: The Collection Called “Balcony”
chapters.desc: A year after the boat. Therapy on Tuesdays. A florist from the Walled City married to her brother-in-law. And a collection about the worst night of her life, which she models for exactly one person, piece by piece.
chapters.epigraph: “Now I know you.”

chapters.title: The Paris Show
chapters.desc: Six days before the presentation, a rival house shows a coat-collar necklace that is hers, line for line. Someone sold her sketches. Her atelier is in pieces. She has three nights. He is in the front row, and does not look at his phone.
chapters.epigraph: “Not everything important has to be seen by everyone.”

chapters.title: Her Parents Ask for Tickets
chapters.desc: After Paris, everyone wants to see the collection in Asia. A letter arrives in her mother’s handwriting asking for two seats. Aurelia sends them. In the back row. Then her father comes to the front anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “Keep it as long as you like.”

chapters.title: He Takes a Day Off
chapters.desc: For the first time in eleven years, he switches off his phone at midnight and does not switch it back on. Nobody in the Syndicate knows what to do. She has planned the day. It involves a chess board, a bucket of ice, and rules.
chapters.epigraph: “Tomorrow, you belong to me.”

chapters.title: The Necklace She Makes for Him
chapters.desc: It isn’t jewellery. It’s a tag. Plain gold, on a plain chain, with three lines engraved on it in her hand, for a man who has spent his whole life waiting to be taken down the stairs.
chapters.epigraph: “Then I’ll always leave the light on.”

chapters.title: Her Father Falls
chapters.desc: Shenzhen. Leverage. Four towers nobody will buy. Permits that won’t come. In eight weeks the Song Group goes from the second-richest family in the city to a story in the newspapers. Her father calls her at two in the morning. Her mother does not.
chapters.epigraph: “Go and get your father.”

chapters.title: Six in the Morning
chapters.desc: A locked drawer her mother never opened in front of anyone. Eleven bankers around one table. And a lane in the Western District at six o’clock, where two people stand side by side and watch a grey man walk down his own steps.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m hungry.”

chapters.title: Number One, By Her Own Rules
chapters.desc: 2024. A collection called “Seconda”, made from every second place she ever came. A prize in Geneva that nobody from Asia has ever won. Her parents in the front row, and a daughter who does not look for them once. And afterwards, in a hotel suite above the lake, a medal on a ribbon and a man who is not allowed to touch it.
chapters.epigraph: “Because I don’t need to rename the past to be proud of what I made out of it.”

chapters.title: Renewing the Contract
chapters.desc: Ten years to the day. Clause eleven says she may rewrite every clause. She has been drafting for a year. He has been preparing for longer, and he has a counter-offer, and a pen, and a book that cost a back-room doctor three days of stitches.
chapters.epigraph: “You only have to keep asking.”

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sets the Price
chapters.desc: Epilogue. October. The house on the Peak, bought at auction by a woman who did not tell anyone she was bidding. A party for her father’s seventieth. The same balcony. A different coat. And the same man, standing at the end of it in the dark.
chapters.epigraph: “To the woman who sets the price.”

chapters.title: Floral vs. Jewelry, Round Forty-One
chapters.desc: A charity lunch. One centrepiece budget. Two women who were first and second at school, and who have not stopped keeping score. Their husbands sit at the end of the table and say nothing, which is the most dangerous thing either of them can do.
chapters.epigraph: “Because I meant it.”

chapters.title: He Has Never Been Late. Today He Was Late.
chapters.desc: Seven o’clock. A dinner reservation he made himself. Seven-fifteen. Seven-thirty. His phone goes to voicemail. Zhao’s phone goes to voicemail. For forty minutes, Aurelia Chen finds out exactly how much of her is still sitting in a corridor outside an ICU.
chapters.epigraph: “Thirty-one minutes late.”

chapters.title: What the Don’s Assistant Puts Up With
chapters.desc: Qian has worked for Chen Si for twelve years. He has two drawers of antacids, a spreadsheet titled “Clause Nine Scheduling Conflicts”, and a theory that the most dangerous man in the city is completely, catastrophically, embarrassingly in love. A week in his life.
chapters.epigraph: “Because I have a very difficult job.”

chapters.title: Blood Brothers Go Anniversary Shopping
chapters.desc: Two of the most feared men in the city. One shopping centre. Three hours before closing. Zhao’s anniversary is on Friday and he has bought nothing; Chen Si’s was on Sunday and he has bought nothing either.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d choose you again.”

chapters.title: She Loses at Mahjong to the Quiet Sister
chapters.desc: Aurelia Chen has not lost a game of mahjong since she was nineteen. Elowen’s quiet sister has not said more than eleven words to her in five years. One Lunar New Year, one table, four players, and a husband standing behind his wife’s chair who is enjoying this far too much.
chapters.epigraph: “You laughed.”

chapters.title: The Sewer, Nineteen Years Ago
chapters.desc: Chen Si has told this story once, to nobody, in his head, every night for nineteen years. Tonight his wife asks about the scar on his arm, and he tells it out loud. Block C. The riot. A boy who came down off the top bunk without deciding to. And half a kilometre of freezing water in the dark.
chapters.epigraph: “Brothers.”

chapters.title: Her Rules for Galas
chapters.desc: The Shen Foundation gala, December 2025, from the other side of the room. Eleven rules, written on cream paper in red ink and slipped into her husband’s pocket at six o’clock. He has annotated every one. In black. In the car.
chapters.epigraph: “I am never bored when you are talking.”

chapters.title: He Reads Her Reviews
chapters.desc: Every review. Every one. Since 2019. In a folder on his laptop called “Rotterdam (Q3)” so that nobody will ever open it. And one night she finds out that he does not only read them. He answers them. Under a name she would recognise anywhere.
chapters.epigraph: “I do what she asks.”

chapters.title: Milan in August
chapters.desc: The city is empty. Everyone who matters has gone to the lakes. The palazzo where they were married is closed for the summer and she has the only key. There is a problem, though, and it is clause ten: the safe word is the name of the city they are standing in, and every waiter in Milan keeps saying it.
chapters.epigraph: “Only if necessary.”

chapters.title: The Ring She Designed Herself
chapters.desc: For three weeks, her husband gets out of bed at two in the morning and comes back at five smelling of polish. Aurelia Chen does not do jealousy. Aurelia Chen follows him anyway, in silk pyjamas and a coat, with a gun in her bag, and finds him somewhere she never expected: at her own bench.
chapters.epigraph: “Then it is perfect.”

chapters.title: A Normal Evening, Attempted
chapters.desc: Elowen and Aurelia book their husbands six hours off, and Eliana diverts every call to either man until eleven. Zhao and Chen Si go bowling, walk out of half a film, and eat noodles at the stall at the mouth of the old-town alley where they came out with cut palms in January 2010.
chapters.epigraph: “He’s allowed to watch a film.”

extras.title: Lo Prometto
extras.line: Eleven pages in red, signed at her counter. Then thirty-seven nights of learning to promise in Italian, without her knowing.

extras.title: Eleven Days
extras.line: The night he lost the argument. He hands her his phone and doesn’t tell her the code. He says she already knows it.

descs.en: He made a rule: the two of them stay flat, like a line on a graph. She gave the line an end date, drew an atom for every day until it, and a week later he kissed her on the back stairs.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Dr. Miles Wei, thirty-one, lectures in physics and holds office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Shen Yu Jie, the best mind in his department, comes on Wednesdays. Every Wednesday. With problems she has already solved.

He has one rule: nothing happens while she’s a student in his department. He draws it on his chalkboard as a flat line. She adds an end date: 20 June, 16:00. Then she gives him a calendar two hundred and fifty-five squares long, with a wildly inaccurate atom in every square.

He counts them twice. A week later, the rule doesn’t survive the back stairs.

Lecturer and student (he never teaches her) · Grumpy and sunshine · Clever people in love · Complete in four volumes, plus ten side stories

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers.

A gentle book, with some hard moments:

• A parent’s emotional control, including being cut off and made to leave home

• Online gossip about a student’s degree

• Coming out to a family at the dinner table

• A high fever

• A secret relationship between a lecturer and a student in his department, later declared. He never teaches, supervises or marks her

• Love scenes on the page

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Miles walked into Thorns for one scene, dropped his clicker, asked Elowen if she was happy, and wouldn’t leave my head. This is his book.

I wanted a love story where the most romantic thing anyone does is take the other person’s mind seriously. The physics is real and kept at story level: harmonic oscillators, entropy as counting, graphene under strain, and black holes made in water tanks, which real laboratories build.

The jokes are, regrettably, also real.

characters.title: Characters

chars.name: Dr. Miles Wei
chars.appearance: Clean-cut and quietly beautiful. Soft brown hair with a fringe, fair skin, gentle eyes behind thin round glasses, a boyish face that looks younger than he is. Black turtlenecks and dark blazers. Smells of chalk, old paper and coffee.
chars.personality:
Literal and deadpan; terrible puns delivered with total seriousness
Stopped laughing at seventeen, after a library fight over his notebook
One rule — nothing happens while she is a student in his department
chars.strengths:
Takes other people’s minds seriously
Kind in small, exact ways
chars.weaknesses:
Retreats into carefulness when he’s frightened
No idea he is handsome
chars.favHabit: Sticky notes with physics jokes on her tea, every Wednesday

chars.name: Shen Yu Jie
chars.appearance: Radiant. Long dark-brown hair with a middle part, big bright doe eyes, rosy lips always about to laugh. A white shirt under a black blazer. Smells of peach and strawberry sweets.
chars.personality:
Bold, bright and very funny
Comes to office hours on Wednesdays with problems she has already solved
The ‘Perfect Jewel’ of a family that expects her to marry well
