glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Wednesday — The day Yu Jie comes to office hours, which are on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
The harmonic oscillator — The problem she brings on her first Wednesday. Its lowest energy, ½ħω, is never zero: nothing is ever completely at rest.
Lecture Theatre C — Where Miles teaches second-year quantum mechanics at ten, to a hundred and forty students.
The rule — Miles’s one rule: not while she is a student in his department.
20 June, 16:00 — The end of the interval: graduation. Written in chalk in the corner of his board, and left there.
The sticky notes — His physics jokes on the side of her tea (yellow), her answers on his door (pink).
White Rabbit — The milk sweets he buys her, “on offer”. Also what she saves him as in her phone.
The Perfect Jewel — What her mother calls her in front of guests.
Shen Holdings — Her family’s company. It owns half the harbour and a forty-storey building downtown.
The Shen Foundation — Her family’s charity. Its tree crest is on the door of the physics building.
The glass room — Where their Wednesdays move once he declares the relationship.
Bell Street — The street by the old wall, with the bakery called Ling’s.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Definitely Not Stuck on Quantum Mechanics
chapters.desc: Shen Yu Jie turns up on the wrong day with a problem she has already solved. Dr. Miles Wei solves it anyway, the long way, and keeps the pen she drops.
chapters.epigraph: “Next time, bring a problem you haven’t solved.”

chapters.title: Office Hours Are Tuesdays and Thursdays
chapters.desc: She keeps coming on Wednesdays. He lies about the pen, buys a second mug, and starts leaving the door open.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re right, Miss Shen.”

chapters.title: The Harmonic Oscillator Is Not a Metaphor
chapters.desc: In front of a hundred and forty second-years she asks if zero-point energy applies to people. He answers honestly, and the whole fourth floor knows by lunch.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s never zero.”

chapters.title: The Lecturer Has One Rule
chapters.desc: Miles turns her down with a graph he drew with a metre rule. She adds an end date: the twentieth of June, four o’clock.
chapters.epigraph: “Then you should have drawn it more carefully.”

chapters.title: A Countdown Disguised as a Semester
chapters.desc: Yu Jie makes a countdown calendar with an atom for every day. Miles finds it, counts the squares twice, and asks to kiss her on the back stairs.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m waiting because I want to.”

chapters.title: The Coffee Cup Physics Jokes Were Not Flirting
chapters.desc: A joke on a sticky note starts a war, Dr. Ling keeps score, and Professor Ruan walks in on the worst joke yet.
chapters.epigraph: “Your jokes are still terrible. Your kisses are not.”

chapters.title: Her Supervisor Is Very Interested
chapters.desc: Professor Ruan warns Yu Jie on the smoking balcony, then climbs to the fourth floor to warn Miles. He answers by reading four papers on her thesis.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re my favourite boundary condition.”

chapters.title: A Study Group of One
chapters.desc: She drags him to a Saturday study group, and it goes well until the head of department walks in. Miles runs, then waits fifty-six minutes for her at the bike rack.
chapters.epigraph: “Just look at me first, so I know you’re coming back.”

chapters.title: He Gets Sick and Nobody Notices
chapters.desc: Miles is sick and nobody notices except Yu Jie, who turns up with soup, a thermometer and oranges, and meets his sister on speakerphone.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re allowed to need someone, you know.”

chapters.title: He Laughs in a Seminar
chapters.desc: Yu Jie takes apart a visiting professor’s slide in the seminar, and Miles laughs out loud for the first time in fourteen years. Then an invitation arrives with her family’s crest on it.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m glad it was me.”

chapters.title: A Rented Suit
chapters.desc: He looks like he’s about to defend a thesis. His sister takes over. Dr. Ling provides croissants and terrible advice.
chapters.epigraph: “Up here I’m just loud.”

chapters.title: The Foundation Gala
chapters.desc: The Perfect Jewel at the top of the stairs. Two married women who recognise him across the room. And a very large man by the pillar, glaring.
chapters.epigraph: “Look at me again when you can.”

chapters.title: Not Jealous of Women Married to Dangerous Men
chapters.desc: She is a little jealous. She would like that noted privately. Then Aurelia Chen corners her in the powder room.
chapters.epigraph: “He laughed for you.”

chapters.title: She Asks Him One Question
chapters.desc: Five years ago he asked her on a balcony. Tonight, on a terrace over the harbour, she asks him back.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m happy on Wednesdays.”

chapters.title: The Diplomat Her Mother Chose
chapters.desc: Yan Zhiyuan is a perfect match on paper: twenty-nine, five languages, a beautiful waltz. Yu Jie hates paper. Then he offers her a deal.
chapters.epigraph: “She has a life that isn’t you.”

chapters.title: The Slow Way Home
chapters.desc: One in the morning, no coat, silver shoes that hurt. He walks her home the long way through the sleeping city, and stops one block early on purpose.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t be stupid about it.”

chapters.title: The Thesis Draft Covered in Red Pen
chapters.desc: He’s not her supervisor. He reads it anyway, all night, and finds the flaw that would have sunk her in May.
chapters.epigraph: “Your gap doesn’t close.”

chapters.title: Rumours in the Department Kitchen
chapters.desc: A photograph on the student forum. A man’s tuxedo jacket at half past one in the morning. Then Miles hears what the postdocs are saying, and finds out he has a temper after all.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re not responsible for my anger.”

chapters.title: He Recuses Himself
chapters.desc: One page, written at his one table between midnight and four. The most honest document in the history of the department. Then the Wednesday rules change, and Ling Hao brings croissants.
chapters.epigraph: “Physics only was this afternoon.”

chapters.title: She Cries in a Stairwell
chapters.desc: New Year’s Eve dinner at the museum, with the Yans at the table and the forum on her mother’s phone. Not because of him. Because of her mother.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re Yu Jie, and you get to decide what that means.”

chapters.title: The Grant Nobody Applied For
chapters.desc: Five years of funding, a laboratory with a four-metre tank that can make a horizon, and a donor who wants no name. Miles is overjoyed for exactly two days.
chapters.epigraph: “Try being happy before you design the entire building.”

chapters.title: He Finds the Name
chapters.desc: A purpose clause in a trust deed, initialled S.Y.J. Then a diplomat in a perfect suit comes to Thursday office hours with no physics question at all.
chapters.epigraph: “Start by listening. You’re quite good at it when you remember.”

chapters.title: Their First Real Fight
chapters.desc: An intercom by a blue door, in the rain. “You bought me a lab.” “I bought you time.” Both of them are right. That’s the problem.
chapters.epigraph: “I didn’t buy you a lab. I bought you time.”

chapters.title: Two Weeks of Not Speaking
chapters.desc: Wednesdays are empty. He keeps the door open anyway. Ling Hao eats for two. Somewhere in the basement, a water tank is waiting.
chapters.epigraph: “I trust it more than mine.”

chapters.title: She Gives the Money Back
chapters.desc: The fortieth floor of the Shen Building, alone, with four pens in her hair. Her father has never once asked her about an equation. Today, he asks.
chapters.epigraph: “Still angry. Still peeling oranges.”

chapters.title: The Perfect Jewel Says No
chapters.desc: Sunday dinner at the museum, with the Yans, a seating plan for two hundred, and a sample of engagement silk. She puts down her chopsticks. Then the diplomat puts down his.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m a physicist. You can’t wear me.”

chapters.title: Cut Off
chapters.desc: The bank card fails at the canteen. A letter from the family office. Seven days to leave. She packs one suitcase, and finds out what she owns.
chapters.epigraph: “May I hold you?”

chapters.title: He Finds Her a Room
chapters.desc: Not his. A slanted attic above a bakery on Bell Street, a landlady who once threw a rolling pin at a health inspector, and bread at four in the morning. He carries the suitcase, and doesn’t go in.
chapters.epigraph: “Because I chose to stay.”

chapters.title: The Thesis Defence
chapters.desc: Nearly three hours in room 301, with an external examiner from the capital who has a score to settle. Miles waits in the corridor and doesn’t sit down.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t try to be perfect. Try to be precise.”

chapters.title: Graduation Day, 4:01 P.M.
chapters.desc: The ceremony ends at four. Eighty-seven steps from the Great Hall to the fourth floor. The first minute she stops being a student in his department.
chapters.epigraph: “Now there’s nothing between us that needs a line.”

chapters.title: A Proof by Induction
chapters.desc: Sunday, a closed building, a key. Miles asks her out the only way he knows how: on a chalkboard, with a base case, an inductive step, and a very small mistake he made on purpose.
chapters.epigraph: “You haven’t proved your inductive step.”

chapters.title: The First Date Has a Lesson Plan
chapters.desc: Four pages, timed to the minute, with learning objectives. She reads it, folds it into a paper plane, and takes him to the night market instead.
chapters.epigraph: “You forgot to ask me what I wanted to do.”

chapters.title: Holding Hands in Public
chapters.desc: Across the campus in July, past the canteen, the library café and the department kitchen. He keeps checking whether anyone is looking. Everyone is. Then a society photographer gets the picture the forum never did.
chapters.epigraph: “Then you don’t have to protect me from people looking at us.”

chapters.title: She Gets a Job
chapters.desc: A research assistant post in the capital, five hours north. He asks her what she wants, and makes himself listen to the answer. Then the last night of August, the door of the staff flat, and a question he asks at every step.
chapters.epigraph: “Then it’ll be hard.”

chapters.title: Distance Is Just a Variable
chapters.desc: The 18:20 and the 21:10. Calls at midnight. A whiteboard screwed to his kitchen wall. A storm, a cancelled train, a handsome postdoc, and a black hole made of water that finally holds.
chapters.epigraph: “I wanted to be the first thing you saw.”

chapters.title: Her Mother Comes to Tea
chapters.desc: No warning, no appointment, pale grey silk on a basement ramp. Mrs. Shen inspects the physics lecturer, his tank, and his only clean mug. He explains entropy. She brings something she was supposed to have thrown away.
chapters.epigraph: “She talks as if the question were the point, not the answer.”

chapters.title: He Meets His Own Past
chapters.desc: A flower shop in the Walled City on a Saturday in May. Elowen and Aurelia, together, at last on the same side, telling him he finally chose correctly. And a glass globe that has been quietly setting the roses on fire.
chapters.epigraph: “You give them to somebody. It isn’t physics.”

chapters.title: The Apartment With Two Desks
chapters.desc: A one-line letter to the Head of Department. Two flights up on Bell Street. Two second-hand desks that face each other, and a cactus that moves house in a bicycle basket.
chapters.epigraph: “Of course I counted. I’m a physicist.”

chapters.title: A Ring Hidden in a Problem Set
chapters.desc: The second Wednesday of September, two years on, 3:47 p.m. Three problems on graph paper, a man who is a very bad liar, and a 113th sticky note.
chapters.epigraph: “You know the distance. You measured it three times.”

chapters.title: Quod Erat Demonstrandum
chapters.desc: Epilogue. Two red booklets in the morning. A garden behind the Hall of Science at 4:01 in the afternoon. A blackboard on an easel, a cake covered in Bohr atoms, and a proof that is finally finished.
chapters.epigraph: “Hello, wife.”

chapters.title: Who Hid His Glasses (Again)
chapters.desc: A short investigation, conducted by Dr. Ling Hao, into the fourteenth disappearance of a pair of glasses on Bell Street. There is one obvious suspect. There is also a motive nobody expected.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re the reason I come home.”

chapters.title: The Night She Made Him Dance in the Empty Lab
chapters.desc: Midnight in the basement of the east wing. One pair of headphones, two people, a horizon holding in a tank of water, and a man who has never danced in his life.
chapters.epigraph: “You’ve stopped a black hole for a cork.”

chapters.title: He Calculates Before Holding Hands
chapters.desc: The second date. A cinema, a shared armrest, and a man with a napkin and a pencil in the dark, working out the optimal moment. She has already done the calculation. Hers is shorter.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to ask the universe for permission.”

chapters.title: The Sticky Note Archive
chapters.desc: For his thirty-fourth birthday, she gives him a binder. A hundred and twelve sticky notes, catalogued, dated, cross-referenced, and annotated. Some of them he doesn’t remember writing. One of them she never showed him.
chapters.epigraph: “Some things take longer to say.”

chapters.title: An Arms Dealer Is Glaring at Me From Across the Room
chapters.desc: The Shen Foundation gala, from inside Miles’s head. A running log of one arms dealer’s stare, the reunion he has spent five years being embarrassed about, and the moment the glaring changed direction.
chapters.epigraph: “Then she really doesn’t look like she wants to run.”

chapters.title: He Tries to Text With Emojis
chapters.desc: The long-distance year, as told through a phone. The atom is not romantic. The cactus is a cry for help. And one message, at 2:14 in the morning, that needed no emoji at all.
chapters.epigraph: “Next time just tell me you’re lonely.”

chapters.title: She Teaches First Years
chapters.desc: Doctoral student, first-year problem class, Thursday mornings, room 104. She is terrifying. They are terrified. By November, there is a queue outside the door on the wrong day.
chapters.epigraph: “Because you’re good at explaining hard things.”

chapters.title: The Department Christmas Party
chapters.desc: The first department party Miles Wei has attended in seven years. There is a quiz. He wins it. There is also karaoke, a secret gift exchange and a dance-off with the Head of Department. She wins everything else.
chapters.epigraph: “I enjoyed watching you.”

chapters.title: Physics Puns, Ranked
chapters.desc: A speech given at the first wedding anniversary dinner, in the back room of a dumpling stall at a night market, by the woman who has heard them all. Fifteen jokes. Ranked. With notes.
chapters.epigraph: “I keep all your notes. It isn’t an endorsement.”

chapters.title: Sixteen, at the Back of the Class
chapters.desc: A boy at the back of Mr. Hui’s advanced class who does impressions of the teacher, a tired girl at the end of his table, a girl who reads his notebook out loud, and eight days that taught him to stop wanting things. And the man who, fourteen years later, unlearned it.
chapters.epigraph: “That isn’t a choice, son. That’s a hiding place.”

extras.title: Still Here
extras.line: The attic over Ling’s bakery. He has gone down for the last box and left his phone under her new lamp. Eighteen days, and what he did instead of writing.

extras.title: Problem Set
extras.line: August to September, two years after a purple pen. He has decided. He has not decided how. He starts on paper.

descs.en: She married the arms dealer to protect her father. He has never stopped wondering whether she married him for love.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Lin Elowen arranges flowers in the Walled City. Her father moves cargo for Zhao Zhendong, the arms dealer the whole city is afraid of. When three of Zhao’s containers are seized and her father takes the blame, Elowen walks into Zhao’s office at the Iron Docks and asks him to marry her.

She brings a contract. Three pages, in her own handwriting. Separate rooms. Her own shop. You don’t touch me unless I ask. He signs it without a word.

He knows why she wants him, and it isn’t love. He would burn the city down for her anyway. What he can’t do is ask the one question that matters: did she ever choose him?

Marriage of convenience · Morally grey hero · He falls first · Complete in four volumes, plus ten side stories

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers.

This is a dark romance. The love story is tender; the world around it isn’t. It includes:

• The arms trade, including weapons sold to militias that use child soldiers

• Torture and killing by the hero, on the page

• Unwanted touching at a dinner table

• Arson and serious burns

• A shooting at the shop with a child present

• A gunshot wound treated at home without anaesthetic

• Child abuse in a character’s past, described briefly, and a prison riot

• Grief for a mother who died giving birth

• Love scenes between the married couple, on the page

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
After The Softest Kind of Love I wanted to write the other kind: a love that’s quiet because it’s so big, between two people who aren’t soft at all.

Zhao is not a good man, and this book doesn’t pretend he is. Elowen knows exactly what he does. What she doesn’t know, for a long time, is what to do about the most frightening man in the city sleeping outside her door so she’ll never have to wonder where he is.

The flower-shop details are real: the four o’clock market, stems cut on the slant, a cooler kept just above freezing. Thank you for reading.

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Elowen’s — Elowen’s flower shop in the Walled City. She painted the sign herself at nineteen.
The Walled City — The old quarter where the Lin family lives and the shop stands. Narrow streets, stairs, umbrellas.
The Iron Docks — The port where Zhao Zhendong does business, and where Lin Jian’s three containers were seized.
The house on the hill — Zhao’s house. Too many locks, two nameless dogs, and one door with no key for her.
The armory — The locked room under the house. A code for if she needs to hide; later, a key for if she just wants to come in.
The contract — Their marriage agreement. Page two, line six: he doesn’t touch her unless she asks.
Block C — The youth detention wing where Zhao met Chen Si at fifteen. He carries the scar of its winter riot.
Middlemist’s Red — A camellia thought to survive in only two places in the world. Everyone says there might be a third.
The paper twins — The Lin family’s buried secret about Raiden and Evangeline.
The Red Notice — The international alert issued with Zhao’s face on it.
The Velde deal — The biggest arms deal Zhao was ever offered, for a highland militia that uses child soldiers. He cancels it.

extras.title: The Fourteenth Key
extras.line: His study, the first sixteen days of March. She has thirteen keys to this house. He is deciding about the last one.

extras.title: Face Down
extras.line: The morning after he walked out of her shop. His phone lights up on his side of the bed, and she knows the code.

chapters.title: The Arms Dealer Who Bought Every Flower in the Shop
chapters.desc: It’s raining, it’s nearly closing time, and the man her father works for buys every flower in the shop so he can wait there for her father’s call.
chapters.epigraph: “Then keep looking.”

chapters.title: Her Father Owes Three Containers
chapters.desc: Her father has lost three containers that weren’t carrying farm machinery, and he has two weeks. Elowen takes the key to his files and finds one letter.
chapters.epigraph: “I know exactly who he is.”

chapters.title: The Florist Who Read His Shipping Routes
chapters.desc: She takes two buses to the Iron Docks to tell Zhao who sold his route. The man she means is sitting on the desk the whole time.
chapters.epigraph: “I sell flowers, Mr. Zhao.”

chapters.title: A Proposal Made Like a Business Deal
chapters.desc: Old Lau ends up in hospital and her father hires a gun he can’t pay for. So Elowen writes three pages of terms and asks Zhao to marry her.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re negotiating my whole life. It seemed fair.”

chapters.title: Married at the Registry on a Tuesday
chapters.desc: She buys ranunculus, takes the household register and marries him at the registry on a Tuesday. The ring is two sizes too big.
chapters.epigraph: “Not yet. I like it heavy.”

chapters.title: The House on the Hill Has Too Many Locks
chapters.desc: She moves into his concrete house with her mother’s lemon tree and names his dogs. In the basement, behind the lock she has no key for, he asks before he kisses her.
chapters.epigraph: “Good evening, Mrs. Zhao.”

chapters.title: Breakfast With a Man Who Eats Standing Up
chapters.desc: She makes him sit down to dinner. He takes her van keys and drives her to the market at four, and she kisses him at the shop door without asking.
chapters.epigraph: “Every stem. Every order. Two years.”

chapters.title: The Other Wife Hears the News
chapters.desc: Aurelia comes to gloat that their husbands are brothers, and leaves with a commission. That night Zhao wants to know which bus the physics boy took.
chapters.epigraph: “There was someone at school, though.”

chapters.title: The First Dinner as His Wife
chapters.desc: Her first dinner as his wife. A broker puts his hand on her knee under the table, and her husband puts a knife through it.
chapters.epigraph: “Because I don’t know what else to do tonight.”

chapters.title: The Night the Delivery Van Burned
chapters.desc: Someone sets fire to her van with Xiao Pan standing next to it. Zhao goes to the Qiu brothers’ warehouse and comes home with a burn she holds under the cold tap.
chapters.epigraph: “Hands under. Keep them there.”

chapters.title: The Night She Asks Him to Stay
chapters.desc: A typhoon, a fever and a power cut. She asks him to stay, and in the morning she asks for more.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m glad you lived.”

chapters.title: Page Two, Line Six
chapters.desc: A week of him not touching her. Then she leaves a thermometer by his soup, says “page two, line six,” and this time nobody has a fever.
chapters.epigraph: “I never miss the market.”

chapters.title: The Florist’s Husband Is Not Allowed Behind the Counter
chapters.desc: Her husband starts coming to work and her takings drop by a third. She puts up house rules. He breaks rule two in four days and gets punished in the cooler.
chapters.epigraph: “Then I’ll keep sweeping until it does.”

chapters.title: Thorns at Six in the Morning
chapters.desc: He learns to strip roses and bleeds on two hundred of them. Chen Si comes in for anniversary flowers and finds his brother in her apron.
chapters.epigraph: “Then I’ll do the other three hundred and ninety-something like this.”

chapters.title: The Rare Flower He Should Not Have Bought
chapters.desc: She reads him a paragraph about the rarest camellia in the world. Three weeks later the hill it grows on is in her name.
chapters.epigraph: “You can’t buy me a hill.”

chapters.title: The Estate in the Rain
chapters.desc: An old tea estate, a man who won’t sell his flower, a shooting lesson on a wet terrace, and two days of rain with the road washed out.
chapters.epigraph: “Then let me take my time.”

chapters.title: Her Father Comes to Dinner
chapters.desc: Her father comes to dinner at last. Zhao cooks her mother’s fish for him, and Lin Jian tells him he was only ever the price.
chapters.epigraph: “You can say what you like about me. Not about her. Not at my table.”

chapters.title: The Shop Gets a New Floor
chapters.desc: Raiden puts a steel room under the tulips. Over the hole in her floor, Zhao tells her brother he loves her. She hears it from the doorway.
chapters.epigraph: “This light stays on. I’ll come.”

chapters.title: A Reunion Invitation With One Name on It
chapters.desc: The school turns sixty and Miles Wei is giving the speech. At two in the morning she finds her husband reading his papers.
chapters.epigraph: “You come with me. Plus one.”

chapters.title: The Arms Dealer Is Absolutely Fine About the Physics Lecturer
chapters.desc: Zhao borrows Xiao Pan’s FLOWER POWER hoodie and goes to the physics lecture in disguise. Chen Si finds him at the back.
chapters.epigraph: “I liked the coffee cup.”

chapters.title: The Reunion, Table Nine
chapters.desc: The reunion. Aurelia fixes Miles’s bow tie, Miles asks Elowen if she’s happy, and then he walks up to the man by the wall without knowing who he is.
chapters.epigraph: “She doesn’t look like she wants to run.”

chapters.title: Two Women, One Gala, Zero Ceasefire
chapters.desc: The Chen Foundation gala. Qiu Wen crushes her peony and she puts a knife to his knuckles and asks after his brother’s hands. Then Zhao dances, very badly, on purpose.
chapters.epigraph: “How are your brother’s hands?”

chapters.title: The Question He Almost Asks
chapters.desc: In the car home from the gala he gets as far as her name. On their first anniversary she gives him a camellia from the hill, he gives her the key to the armory, and in the middle of the night his phone rings.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s for if you just want to come in.”

chapters.title: A Red Notice With His Face on It
chapters.desc: His phone won’t stop ringing and he’s stopped eating, so every night she takes a bowl down to the basement. Then the boy who used to sit on her wall walks into the shop as a detective and tells her which footnote to read.
chapters.epigraph: “Then stop sending me away.”

chapters.title: The Order She Wouldn’t Fill
chapters.desc: A man with a forgettable face orders two funeral wreaths with her husband’s name on the ribbon, and she rings the detective first. Zhao walks out on her for the first time, and comes back from Chen Si’s very late with an apology.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re always here on Wednesdays.”

chapters.title: Glass
chapters.desc: Nobody says the date out loud. He buys her soy milk at the market, a little girl wants sunflowers with a yellow ribbon for her grandmother, and then a car comes down the street too slowly.
chapters.epigraph: “He’s my husband.”

chapters.title: Nobody Else Touches Her
chapters.desc: He sends her sister out of the bathroom and puts the strips on her neck himself, shaking the whole time. Before dawn he tells her how long he’ll be gone, and she doesn’t say don’t.
chapters.epigraph: “Come back.”

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.desc: Forty-eight hours, from his side. A boy who stole a car, a driver in the harbour, a shooter on a landing, and a koi pond on the coast.
chapters.epigraph: “For the widow.”

chapters.title: He Came Home Washed
chapters.desc: He comes home scrubbed raw and she asks if anyone’s dead. He tells her the truth, comes apart on the kitchen floor, and agrees that her father is hers to deal with.
chapters.epigraph: “Is anyone dead?”

chapters.title: She Goes to Her Father’s House
chapters.desc: She leaves her husband asleep with a second hair tie on his wrist and goes to the Walled City. Eliana has already found the man who sold her Wednesdays, and a message that says their father knew.
chapters.epigraph: “Is that about me?”

chapters.title: The Man in Her Father’s Office
chapters.desc: Feng is in the outer office eating sunflower seeds. Inside, her father finally tells her what he was paid to do with an infant in a silk blanket, while her husband cuts her tulips at the wrecked shop.
chapters.epigraph: “Then you can put me to bed yourself.”

chapters.title: What a Daughter Owes
chapters.desc: Chen Si takes Feng away and nobody dies. At the kitchen table her father tells them all about the paper twins. Evangeline already knew.
chapters.epigraph: “I wasn’t being protected. I was being hidden.”

chapters.title: A Phone Call From the Top Floor
chapters.desc: She can’t go home tonight, so Aurelia takes her forty-four floors up, runs a bath and tells her about the boat. Her husband sits on the stairs till morning.
chapters.epigraph: “Tomorrow, don’t let me sleep. Page two, line six.”

chapters.title: She Comes Back Through the Front Door
chapters.desc: He spends the whole night on the bottom stair with the dogs, sure she isn’t coming back. She comes home in Aurelia’s clothes, tells him everything, and he asks her to save the last thing for a boring day.
chapters.epigraph: “If you’re going to say it, say it on a boring day.”

chapters.title: A Shipment With Children’s Names on It
chapters.desc: Two years on, there’s a plant room with a tap at the height of her hip and a black card she can’t give back. Then he brings home the biggest deal he’s ever been offered and asks her to read it, every page.
chapters.epigraph: “Because of the names.”

chapters.title: He Cancels the Deal
chapters.desc: Chen Si says there are children in all of it, Bao tells her about his little brother, and Granny Yip says soft men live longer. Then the man who runs the northern warehouses calls her husband a dog in front of her, and she turns a page.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m using my husband.”

chapters.title: The Buyer Does Not Take No Well
chapters.desc: A warehouse burns with a florist’s card left on the gate, and Maartens flies in to ask for a meeting at the old shipyard. She can’t tell her husband not to go, so she moves the fish to the front of the fridge.
chapters.epigraph: “Not like this. You promised me a boring one.”

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.desc: Three days in the armory with his coat and a gun. Everyone who loves her comes to the steel door, and she won’t open it for any of them.
chapters.epigraph: “Every way back into the house.”

chapters.title: He Crawled the Last Mile
chapters.desc: He crawls home up the hill with a bullet in his side. Elara brings two bags of stolen hospital supplies, and Elowen holds his face on the kitchen table for two hours.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m late. For dinner.”

chapters.title: “I Stained Your Life”
chapters.desc: Two days of fever. He wakes once, says sorry for everything, and falls asleep on the question he’s been carrying for three years.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re not the stain, Zhendong. You’re the wall. You keep it out.”

chapters.title: The Question He Never Asked
chapters.desc: Two weeks after the shipyard, on the most boring day there has ever been, he finally asks why she married him. She tells him the truth, and makes him wait for the rest.
chapters.epigraph: “Obviously yes. You idiot.”

chapters.title: The Flower in His Lapel
chapters.desc: Closing time, rain, and a camellia from the mountain in his lapel. She tells him why she stayed, and he finally says it back.
chapters.epigraph: “I loved you first.”

chapters.title: Closing Half an Empire
chapters.desc: He starts shutting down the worst of the business, slowly. Chen Si lies for him, Elowen keeps the books, one man finds out what happens if he cheats, and Wei Long gets a list.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to be useful to get a place here.”

chapters.title: The Wedding They Eloped From
chapters.desc: Three and a half years after the registry, they have the wedding in the flower shop. Raiden walks in with a wife nobody knew about, and Baba asks about the lemon tree.
chapters.epigraph: “How is the lemon tree?”

chapters.title: Every Flower in the Shop
chapters.desc: Five years on, it starts to rain over the Docks and he walks out of a meeting without his umbrella. He’s on her mat at closing time, and a girl outside is looking at the tulips in the window.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d pay that every night. Just to stand on that mat again.”

chapters.title: The Arms Dealer Tries to Arrange Flowers
chapters.desc: The florist has a fever on Mother’s Day, so her husband takes her forty-three orders. He measures every bow with a ruler, and then he gets to the one that says use your judgment.
chapters.epigraph: “Like the person.”

chapters.title: The Delivery Boy Who Saw Too Much
chapters.desc: Xiao Pan has worked at Elowen’s for five years and would like it on the record that he never wanted to see any of it. A numbered list, the cooler not included, and the best tip he ever got.
chapters.epigraph: “For looking after her. Before I knew how.”

chapters.title: Please Tell Your Wife to Stop
chapters.desc: Chen Si rings in the middle of the night because Aurelia has been pacing the living room in her silk robe for two hours. Elowen has bought the building next door, he gave Aurelia sapphires, and somehow he’s losing.
chapters.epigraph: “She wants to win something.”

chapters.title: Anniversary Math
chapters.desc: She goes looking for a pen and finds two notebooks in his drawer: every date since the night it rained, and a number in the corner of every page.
chapters.epigraph: “I thought I could at least keep the dates.”

chapters.title: Fifteen Years Ago, Block C
chapters.desc: January, fifteen years ago. A riot in Block C, a sharpened bed slat, and Chen Si dragging him half a kilometre through the drains into the snow. Then his wife finds him awake at two.
chapters.epigraph: “Then don’t leave.”

chapters.title: The Ring Was Too Heavy
chapters.desc: Three weeks before the real wedding her ring vanishes from the dish by the till, and Bao is a terrible liar. Then she reads the inside.
chapters.epigraph: “Now you won’t take it off.”

chapters.title: The Youngest Sister Sleeps Over at the Big House
chapters.desc: The heating breaks in the Walled City, so Eliana spends a weekend at the house on the hill. She takes Zhao’s security apart in thirty-eight minutes, and he has never been happier.
chapters.epigraph: “About where we stand.”

chapters.title: The Boss’s Wife Does the Armory’s Accounts
chapters.desc: From the private diary of Mr. Yao, Zhao’s accountant, the year the boss’s wife starts keeping the books. She finds his four-year-old mistake with a pencil, and he never quite recovers.
chapters.epigraph: “This is perfect.”

chapters.title: The Language of Flowers, Studied in Secret
chapters.desc: He buys her yellow roses, and she tells him what yellow means. So he buys a very old book and starts again, one stem at a time.
chapters.epigraph: “Because someone thinks you’re lovely.”

chapters.title: Valentine’s Day in a Flower Shop
chapters.desc: Nine hundred roses, one till, and an arms dealer saying “Next.” The customers have never been so polite.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m married. To him.”

descs.en: Lin Xiaoran is dramatic, affectionate, and impossible to handle. Zhou Yichen is patient, gentle, and hopelessly weak against her tears. Somehow, they fit together perfectly.

chapters.desc: He knew she was trouble the moment she started crying—and he still loved her too much to stop spoiling her.
chapters.title: The Boy Who Always Smiled at Her
chapters.epigraph: “Some people are impossible to handle—and impossible not to love.”

chapters.desc: A claw machine, a chance meeting, and one boy who smiled like he already knew she was meant to stay.
chapters.title: Strawberry Milk Confession
chapters.epigraph: “He found her in chaos, and stayed like it was home.”

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen noticed her long before she noticed him—loud, chaotic, impossible to forget—and quietly decided she would become his favorite coincidence.
chapters.title: All Our Coincidences Were Intentional
chapters.epigraph: “Before he ever spoke to her, he had already started choosing her.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran thought she understood Zhou Yichen completely… until she saw what his silence looked like when someone else tried to take his place.
chapters.title: The Day Zhou Yichen Finally Got Jealous
chapters.epigraph: “He was never jealous often—so when he was, even love felt dangerous.”

chapters.desc: She said it over a plate of shrimp, in front of witnesses, without meaning to—and Zhou Yichen was never going to let her take it back.
chapters.title: The First Time She Said “I Love You” Casually
chapters.epigraph: “The biggest words are sometimes the ones that slip out by accident.”

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen almost never gets angry. Then a teammate says the wrong thing about Lin Xiaoran, and he can’t let it go.
chapters.title: The One Time Zhou Yichen Lost His Temper
chapters.epigraph: “Gentle people have a line too. You just don’t see it until someone crosses it.”

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen is leaving on a family trip for seven days. Lin Xiaoran is handling it terribly.
chapters.title: The Week Lin Xiaoran Became Unbearably Clingy
chapters.epigraph: “Seven days isn’t long—unless you’re counting.”

chapters.desc: One week apart, one airport reunion, and Lin Xiaoran is not prepared for how good her boyfriend looks.
chapters.title: The Day Zhou Yichen Came Back Looking Illegal
chapters.epigraph: “Absence makes the heart grow fonder—and apparently the boyfriend more handsome.”

chapters.desc: She only wanted to buy him pastries. She did not plan to get lost without her phone.
chapters.title: The Day Lin Xiaoran Got Horribly Lost
chapters.epigraph: “Some people find their way home with a map. She found hers by being found.”

chapters.desc: Insult Lin Xiaoran and she’ll pout. Insult Zhou Yichen in front of her, and you’d better run.
chapters.title: Xiaoran, Don’t Fight
chapters.epigraph: “She couldn’t fight at all. She fought anyway.”

chapters.desc: Final exams are coming, Lin Xiaoran just scored 43, and her boyfriend is terrifyingly good at math. What could go wrong?
chapters.title: Lin Xiaoran vs Mathematics (A Tragic Story)
chapters.epigraph: “Some battles are lost before they begin. She fought this one anyway.”

chapters.desc: Three weeks of tutoring, one practice test that ends in tears, and a score nobody saw coming.
chapters.title: One Hundred for Love
chapters.epigraph: “Being believed in is its own kind of formula.”

chapters.desc: Months of dating, one nosy question at lunch, and a first kiss that goes almost perfectly.
chapters.title: The First Kiss Was Absolutely Not Smooth
chapters.epigraph: “The best first kisses are never the smooth ones.”

chapters.desc: One weekend of romance dramas, one very specific request, and an empty hallway after practice.
chapters.title: Better Than the Drama
chapters.epigraph: “Real life has no background music. It has something better.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran wanted one proper date. She didn’t expect a street band to describe her relationship out loud.
chapters.title: The Song That Knew Too Much
chapters.epigraph: “Some songs sound like they were written about you. Some actually were.”

chapters.desc: Her cousin and her boyfriend are spending Saturday together. Lin Xiaoran has concerns.
chapters.title: Lin Jun Stole Her Boyfriend for a Day
chapters.epigraph: “The scariest meeting isn’t meeting the parents. It’s meeting the cousin who knows everything.”

chapters.desc: One bad landing in a close game, and Lin Xiaoran learns what real fear feels like.
chapters.title: Don’t Scare Me Like That Again
chapters.epigraph: “Some people love quietly. She loved like a fire alarm.”

chapters.desc: Three weeks off the court. One girlfriend in full nurse mode. Zhou Yichen may not survive his own recovery.
chapters.title: Don’t Limp. I’ll Cry Again.
chapters.epigraph: “The injury healed in weeks. The worry took longer.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran overhears that she’s holding Zhou Yichen back—and starts to wonder if they’re right.
chapters.title: Should We Break Up?
chapters.epigraph: “The cruelest words are the ones we quietly agree with.”

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen eats chili oil like water. Lin Xiaoran decides to build a tolerance. It goes about as well as expected.
chapters.title: You’re Crying Over Chili Oil?
chapters.epigraph: “Love is wanting to share someone’s world, even when it burns.”

chapters.desc: A double date with the rival captain and the girl Xiaoran once fought on the café street. What could go wrong?
chapters.title: Should We Even Be Sitting Together?
chapters.epigraph: “Peace treaties are usually signed over food.”

chapters.desc: Fourteen days to find the perfect gift for a boy who already has everything—and remembers everything.
chapters.title: The Birthday Gift Problem
chapters.epigraph: “The best gifts aren’t bought. They’re remembered.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran has never cooked. Zhou Yichen’s parents are out on Saturday. She’s going to cook anyway.
chapters.title: This Tastes Suspiciously Edible
chapters.epigraph: “The secret ingredient is stubbornness.”

chapters.desc: A sudden downpour, a useless umbrella, and one sentence Lin Xiaoran really didn’t mean to say out loud.
chapters.title: Holding Hands Is Warm, But Hugging in the Rain Is Dangerous
chapters.epigraph: “Some storms are worth getting caught in.”

chapters.desc: A teacher’s wedding, one cream-colored dress, and the evening Zhou Yichen forgot how to talk.
chapters.title: Xiaoran Looks Beautiful Today
chapters.epigraph: “He had seen her every day. He had never seen her like this.”

chapters.desc: One secondhand poetry book. One very dramatic girlfriend. One week nobody at school will ever forget.
chapters.title: Xiaoran Became a Poetry Menace
chapters.epigraph: “Even ordinary afternoons become literature.”

chapters.desc: His first game back after the injury. Scouts in the stands. Lin Xiaoran, holding nothing.
chapters.title: The Game the Scouts Came to See
chapters.epigraph: “Some people worry with their whole body.”

chapters.desc: University offers are arriving for Zhou Yichen. Lin Xiaoran is quietly terrified of where they might take him.
chapters.title: Which Future Includes You?
chapters.epigraph: “Plans change. People stay.”

chapters.desc: One internet question. One very serious girlfriend. Zhou Yichen was not prepared.
chapters.title: Would You Still Love Me If I Was a Capybara?
chapters.epigraph: “Real love answers ridiculous questions sincerely.”

chapters.desc: Lunch at Zhou Yichen’s house, with both his parents home. Lin Xiaoran is not emotionally prepared.
chapters.title: I’m Invited to Zhou Yichen’s House?
chapters.epigraph: “You learn the most about someone from the people who raised them.”

chapters.desc: For her first birthday as his girlfriend, Zhou Yichen plans everything—and remembers something she forgot.
chapters.title: The Birthday Where Zhou Yichen Lost Financial Control
chapters.epigraph: “He remembered the things she forgot she wanted.”

chapters.desc: Xiaoran wants to follow him to university. Yichen says no. Their first real fight about the future.
chapters.title: Somewhere Between Your Dream and Mine
chapters.epigraph: “Love isn’t following someone. It’s finding the place where both of you can grow.”

chapters.desc: The gaokao: two exam venues across the city, one fraction question, and a taxi that took thirty-one minutes.
chapters.title: Two Days in June
chapters.epigraph: “You always know the first step. Write that.”

chapters.desc: Applications are in, results are coming, and four friends are refreshing their portals in the same hour.
chapters.title: The Day Our Futures Arrived
chapters.epigraph: “Some futures arrive all at once.”

chapters.desc: One summer gap, one campus in Shanghai, and a café they’ve already decided is theirs.
chapters.title: Practicing Our Future
chapters.epigraph: “Practice makes the future less frightening.”

chapters.desc: On graduation day, Lin Xiaoran accidentally asks Zhou Yichen to marry her. His answer is worse.
chapters.title: Yichen, Will You Marry Me?
chapters.epigraph: “Some questions are asked too early. Some answers are not.”

chapters.desc: The graduation-day question, from the side of the boy who heard it.
chapters.title: Will You Marry Me? — Zhou Yichen’s Side
chapters.epigraph: “He stayed calm on the outside. He always did.”

chapters.desc: Tang Meilin has been hiding something for three months. Lin Xiaoran is a professional investigator.
chapters.title: Tang Meilin Had a Boyfriend?!
chapters.epigraph: “The quiet ones always have the best secrets.”

chapters.desc: A tiny studio in Shanghai, four flights of stairs, and Lin Xiaoran’s mother has questions for Zhou Yichen.
chapters.title: Moving Day Comes With Parents
chapters.epigraph: “Check twice. She lies the first time.”

chapters.desc: Orientation day, a phone on silent, and the first time in months Zhou Yichen is genuinely angry.
chapters.title: Zhou Yichen Was Actually Angry
chapters.epigraph: “Calm people don’t worry less. They just hide it better.”

chapters.desc: A new university, new friends, and one festival crowd that swallows Lin Xiaoran whole.
chapters.title: Lost Inside the Crowd
chapters.epigraph: “New places change a lot of things. Not who comes looking for you.”

chapters.desc: Xiaoran insists on apologizing to Yichen’s study group—and learns a few things she was never supposed to know.
chapters.title: Lost Inside the Crowd (Part 2)
chapters.epigraph: “Everyone knew. She was the last to find out.”

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen buys a car because of one joke. He is not sorry.
chapters.title: The Day Zhou Yichen Started Looking Expensive
chapters.epigraph: “Some men hold grudges. He held them beautifully.”

chapters.desc: A bored Zhou Yichen, a rainy café, and four traps Lin Xiaoran walks straight into.
chapters.title: Zhou Yichen Was a Psychological Threat at the Café
chapters.epigraph: “Never trust a calm man with nothing to do.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran hates exams. Then Zhou Yichen mentions pandas.
chapters.title: Pass Everything and I’ll Take You to Chengdu
chapters.epigraph: “Zhou Yichen never made promises carelessly.”

chapters.desc: First winter break of university. The old noodle shop, a failed lab report, and Tang Meilin’s boyfriend walks in.
chapters.title: The Four of Us, One Winter Later
chapters.epigraph: “Same time next winter.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran is clingy every day of the year—except the days she actually needs someone.
chapters.title: When Lin Xiaoran Gets Sick, She Stops Acting Like Herself
chapters.epigraph: “You let me spoil you every other day.”

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen joins the university basketball team. Lin Xiaoran discovers he has fans.
chapters.title: Too Many Girls Know Zhou Yichen
chapters.epigraph: “Because when I play seriously, I want you there.”

chapters.desc: Three months, one passed exam season, and the first trip that’s just the two of them.
chapters.title: The Chengdu Promise Finally Happened
chapters.epigraph: “Giant pandas were only the second-best thing in Chengdu.”

chapters.desc: His first university tournament is four days away. Lin Xiaoran has discovered potassium.
chapters.title: The Week Lin Xiaoran Became a Sports Nutrition Expert
chapters.epigraph: “Your body belongs to university basketball now.”

chapters.desc: Number eleven, a stadium full of fans, and a final minute Lin Xiaoran will scream through.
chapters.title: The First Tournament Was Very Bad for Lin Xiaoran’s Heart
chapters.epigraph: “You know what I kept thinking during the game? That you were watching.”

chapters.desc: The team wants to celebrate. Lin Xiaoran plans to slip away. Zhou Yichen has other plans.
chapters.title: “You’re Coming With Me.”
chapters.epigraph: “So why are you acting like you don’t belong beside me?”

chapters.desc: Hotpot, three victory speeches, and a quiet walk home under the streetlights.
chapters.title: After the Celebration, Zhou Yichen Became Too Gentle
chapters.epigraph: “When we won, I searched for you first.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran’s first field assignment. Zhou Yichen moves his schedule to hold her iced tea.
chapters.title: Zhou Yichen Was Completely Useless During the Assignment
chapters.epigraph: “If you got nervous, I wanted to be there already.”

chapters.desc: A national media strategy competition, a month of 2 AM study sessions, and something Lin Xiaoran wants to prove.
chapters.title: Lin Xiaoran’s First Win
chapters.epigraph: “I want to know I can be good at something difficult too.”

chapters.desc: A livestream assignment, thirty identical bottles, and eyeliner—the destroyer of relationships.
chapters.title: Can My Boyfriend Do My Makeup?
chapters.epigraph: “Why is this harder than free throws?”

chapters.desc: Four hours of silence, one genuinely angry boyfriend, and a stuffed panda deployed as a weapon.
chapters.title: The Selfie That Made Zhou Yichen Forget Why He Was Angry
chapters.epigraph: “You cannot send selfies during arguments.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran posts three photos for the first time in months. Zhou Yichen makes the mistake of scrolling down.
chapters.title: Zhou Yichen Read the Comments
chapters.epigraph: “I just didn’t like everyone else liking them too.”

chapters.desc: Finals week, a stress habit nobody noticed, and Zhou Yichen at the campus pharmacy with enough supplies for a minor apocalypse.
chapters.title: Stop Biting Your Lip
chapters.epigraph: “Because you take care of everyone except yourself.”

chapters.desc: Three years together, and Lin Xiaoran has never once seen Zhou Yichen watch basketball. Until 8 AM on a Saturday.
chapters.title: The Terrifying Discovery That Zhou Yichen Was a Nerd
chapters.epigraph: “It’s not nerd things. It’s an organized binder.”

chapters.desc: Zhou Yichen says he doesn’t need anything for his birthday. Lin Xiaoran remembers one sentence from three months ago.
chapters.title: Two Tickets to the Garden
chapters.epigraph: “Of course I remembered.”

chapters.desc: Snow, a pretzel the size of her head, and an envelope that makes Lin Xiaoran shout in a Chinatown noodle shop.
chapters.title: New York Before Tip-Off
chapters.epigraph: “The gift was never the money.”

chapters.desc: Game day at Madison Square Garden. But first, a fashion crisis on Fifth Avenue.
chapters.title: The Day Lin Xiaoran Wanted to Look Grown-Up
chapters.epigraph: “Not cute. Not pretty. Beautiful.”

chapters.desc: A few comments read at 2 AM, two weeks of skipped meals, and a date that ends in a quiet café.
chapters.title: The Day Zhou Yichen Found Out Lin Xiaoran Was Dieting
chapters.epigraph: “Who told you that you needed to change?”

chapters.desc: A thirteen-day family vacation. Lin Xiaoran is a mature adult. Day Three is concerning.
chapters.title: Two Weeks Was Apparently Too Long
chapters.epigraph: “I hate family vacations.”

chapters.desc: A lost French couple, a café near campus, and a language Lin Xiaoran forgot to mention.
chapters.title: The Day Zhou Yichen Discovered His Girlfriend Secretly Spoke French
chapters.epigraph: “The same thing she’d been telling him all along—just in a different language.”

chapters.desc: A peaceful Saturday at the Zhou house, until Mrs. Zhou’s best friend’s daughter walks in calling him “ge.”
chapters.title: The Worst Visitor in Zhou Family History
chapters.epigraph: “The real problem had always been Xiaoran’s own imagination.”

chapters.desc: Lunar New Year at her grandparents’ house, and one uncle with opinions about why she’s dating Zhou Yichen.
chapters.title: The One Thing Lin Xiaoran Could Never Tolerate
chapters.epigraph: “I chose him because he’s Zhou Yichen.”

chapters.desc: Grandma Lin wants to see the boy up close. Uncle Deng will be there. So will the dumplings.
chapters.title: Zhou Yichen Meets the Relatives
chapters.epigraph: “That one’s acceptable.”

chapters.desc: A weekly viewing report, eleven hours of dramas, and the most dangerous thing Zhou Yichen has ever done: change a password.
chapters.title: Netflix vs Zhou Yichen
chapters.epigraph: “You violated my human rights.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran is “extremely busy.” Her lie lasts approximately three minutes.
chapters.title: The World’s Worst Liar
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody who was actually busy sent updates about how busy they were.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran has discovered a new research topic. It has categories, lists, and ratings. Zhou Yichen would like it to stop.
chapters.title: The Internet Was a Mistake
chapters.epigraph: “Do you know how dangerous you are?”

chapters.desc: In his dream, Lin Xiaoran is a famous idol who has never met him. He does not take it well.
chapters.title: The Dream That Made Zhou Yichen Hug Xiaoran at 3 AM
chapters.epigraph: “The one who knew exactly who Zhou Yichen was.”

chapters.desc: Jiayi and Ning want a night out by the river. Lin Xiaoran has never been to a club. Zhou Yichen has, exactly twice.
chapters.title: The First Night Out
chapters.epigraph: “Since we were seventeen.”

chapters.desc: Three rejections in one week, deleted before anyone can ask. She stops saying “guess what” at dinner. He notices.
chapters.title: The Emails She Didn’t Forward
chapters.epigraph: “I made an exception.”

chapters.desc: A summer internship in Beijing. A training camp outside the city. Eight weeks and more than a thousand kilometres.
chapters.title: The Internship in Another City
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t want you to go tomorrow.”

chapters.desc: Shorter calls, one missed night that matters, and a station where this time she’s the one waiting.
chapters.title: The Internship in Another City (Part 2)
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t make yourself smaller just because I’m far away.”

chapters.desc: A point guard from Hangzhou posts one photograph from camp. The whole team sees it. Captain Zhou may never recover.
chapters.title: The Photograph in His Training Bag
chapters.epigraph: “I held it anyway.”

chapters.desc: A man in a dark jacket at the back of the university gym, a message from a professional club, and a very small basketball keychain.
chapters.title: The Scout at the Back of the Gym
chapters.epigraph: “Then you’ll still be Zhou Yichen.”

chapters.desc: While he talks to his coach, a recruiter sits down beside Lin Xiaoran and asks a few questions. She answers every single one.
chapters.title: The Girlfriend Who Didn’t Know She Was Being Interviewed
chapters.epigraph: “That’s why they should ask me.”

chapters.desc: His first professional scrimmage, and his name isn’t called. Somebody’s father made a phone call.
chapters.title: The First Time He Doesn’t Play
chapters.epigraph: “Then keep trying.”

chapters.desc: The third evaluation, the main group at last, and a folder of letters from people who never told him they’d written.
chapters.title: The Player They Almost Overlooked
chapters.epigraph: “I liked that you didn’t let them make you feel small.”

chapters.desc: A new sponsor’s logo on his sleeve, and Zhou Yichen is ready to walk away. Lin Xiaoran goes to dinner with his father instead.
chapters.title: Not Number Seventeen
chapters.epigraph: “I’m going to earn it.”

chapters.desc: Her parents visit without telling her. Her mother inspects his fridge. Her father takes him fishing. Nobody invites her.
chapters.title: Her Parents Come to Shanghai
chapters.epigraph: “You can be their favourite child.”

chapters.desc: Five hours of silence from an away game, and Lin Xiaoran finally learns what twenty-three unread messages feel like from the other side.
chapters.title: The Night His Phone Died
chapters.epigraph: “Once was all I could manage.”

chapters.desc: A schedule planned to the minute, a cup and a fruit bowl, and a sunset that refuses to cooperate.
chapters.title: Four Years, Planned Badly
chapters.epigraph: “That one’s flexible.”

chapters.desc: One street interview, a million views, and a boyfriend who hasn’t posted anything in months.
chapters.title: The Girl on Everyone’s Feed
chapters.epigraph: “Please be kind to her.”

chapters.desc: Winter break at her parents’ house. Her mother has photographs, stories, and absolutely no mercy.
chapters.title: The Little Warrior
chapters.epigraph: “Good night, little warrior.”

chapters.desc: The Media faculty makes a film that makes everyone cry. The Business faculty bankrupts a company. They’re both on the same stage.
chapters.title: The Last Scene Before the Credits
chapters.epigraph: “It only needed another day.”

chapters.desc: His first fan-signing as a Herons player. Someone asks him to sign her arm. Then someone familiar joins the queue.
chapters.title: The Girl at the End of the Queue
chapters.epigraph: “There’s a difference.”

chapters.desc: Lin Xiaoran wants to learn to drive. Zhou Yichen hands her the keys to the car he bought because of one joke.
chapters.title: The Most Expensive Driving Lesson
chapters.epigraph: “It’s a car. Not a family heirloom.”

chapters.desc: Mai Lang invites them onto his channel for a how-well-do-you-know-your-partner quiz. Somebody is going to be exposed.
chapters.title: The Couple Quiz Went Live
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t need a reason to want something.”

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Lin Xiaoran is loud, dramatic, cries easily, and can get lost walking somewhere she’s been twenty times. Zhou Yichen is calm, patient, and very hard not to notice. He fell for her almost right away, and he has been spoiling her ever since.

From their last years of high school to university in Shanghai, The Softest Kind of Love follows the two of them through first dates and bad fights, exams and families, and the slow work of growing up without growing apart.

Main chapters tell the story in order. Side stories are small moments you can read whenever you like.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
This is a gentle romance, but a few chapters include:

• A crude, sexualized remark made about Xiaoran by a classmate (The One Time Zhou Yichen Lost His Temper)

• A physical fight between students (Xiaoran, Don’t Fight)

• A sports injury with some blood and a hospital visit (Don’t Scare Me Like That Again, Don’t Limp. I’ll Cry Again.)

• Hurtful rumors and a brief break-up scare (Should We Break Up?)

• Dieting and skipped meals after hurtful online comments (The Day Zhou Yichen Found Out Lin Xiaoran Was Dieting)

• Mild language and lots of crying

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
I wanted to write the kind of love story I like to read before bed: no cheating, no misunderstanding that drags on for twenty chapters, nobody secretly dying. Just two people who like each other a lot and keep choosing each other, even on the days one of them is being impossible.

Xiaoran is a bit of everyone who has cried over a math test or sulked because their boyfriend was too popular. Yichen is the person a lot of us wish we had, or wish we were—someone who notices when you’ve gone quiet.

Some chapters are silly. Some are soft. A couple of them made me cry a little while writing. Thank you for reading any of them at all.

— 甜慕

descs.en: A trauma surgeon reborn as a governor’s daughter falls for the Emperor’s nephew from a balcony — and then does something very foolish to see him again. A slow, warm historical romance told in stitches, letters and one river.

chapters.title: The Girl on the Balcony
chapters.desc: A general rides through Qingzhou, and a sixteen-year-old with a surgeon’s memory forgets to breathe.
chapters.epigraph: “Come away from there. It is unbecoming to stare at soldiers.” “I’m observing the botanical garden, Mother.” “From memory?”

chapters.title: The Return of Uncle Xiang
chapters.desc: Her uncle, the army’s chief physician, comes home for a few days, and she asks all the wrong questions.
chapters.epigraph: “He has declined every proposal put to him. Why do you ask, Shiyu?” “I was thinking about military logistics.”

chapters.title: The Decision
chapters.desc: There is no sensible way to see him again. So she picks a foolish one.
chapters.epigraph: “I understand what you’re asking. And the answer is no.” — Uncle Xiang, the first time

chapters.title: Discovered
chapters.desc: Four hours hidden in a supply carriage, and then the lid comes off.
chapters.epigraph: “She concealed herself before departure, General.” “In whose carriage?” “…Yours.”

chapters.title: The Interrogation and the Truth
chapters.desc: Accused of being a spy, she has one defence left: the embarrassing truth.
chapters.epigraph: “The enemy’s intelligence assets always say that.” “Do they also say they came to look at you?”

chapters.title: The Medical Tent
chapters.desc: Six weeks, a tent full of wounded men, and a chance to prove she belongs.
chapters.epigraph: “Every case is documented. The General requires it, reviews it, and uses it. It is not optional.” — Uncle Xiang

chapters.title: He Reads the Reports
chapters.desc: Chen Ye lets slip what the General does with her reports in the evenings.
chapters.epigraph: “The reports, certainly. The Chief Physician mentioned they were unusually thorough.” — Chen Ye, choosing his words

chapters.title: The Battle, and What Came After
chapters.desc: The eastern flank breaks, and the tent fills faster than she can count.
chapters.epigraph: “Go directly there and directly back. I will know if you don’t.” “I know you will.”

chapters.title: The Arrow and the Heartbeat
chapters.desc: She stitches the General’s arm, and her hands are steadier than her heart.
chapters.epigraph: “Is it just me, or did the General not take his eyes off her the entire time?” — overheard, outside the command tent

chapters.title: The Hour of the Rabbit
chapters.desc: He tells her to come at dawn to take the stitches out. She is early.
chapters.epigraph: “I revised the estimate based on observed progression. Seven will be sufficient.” — on the stitches, at the hour of the rabbit

chapters.title: The Last Week
chapters.desc: Her last days at the camp, and the men who finally say what they think of her.
chapters.epigraph: “Your time here has been of value to the camp. I wanted you to know I have noted it.” — the General

chapters.title: The Road South
chapters.desc: She rides home without looking back. Almost.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m still deciding whether to be angry with you. Come inside. Cook made the congee you like.” — Lady Ren

chapters.title: Three Years
chapters.desc: A clinic of her own, a nickname she finds excessive, and a life built on purpose.
chapters.epigraph: “The clinic will need a proper sign. Something that looks established.” — Yun Shiyu, seventeen, very sure

chapters.title: Mei Yun
chapters.desc: A fifteen-year-old talks her way into the clinic and notices far too much.
chapters.epigraph: “You receive a letter from your uncle every two weeks.” “He writes regularly.” “I’m just observing.” — Mei Yun, fifteen

chapters.title: The Return
chapters.desc: The northern army comes through Qingzhou with a wounded officer, and asks for the Fairy Physician.
chapters.epigraph: “She’s the Fairy Physician.” — Mei Yun, helpfully, from behind Shiyu’s left shoulder

chapters.title: The Five Days
chapters.desc: She treats Zhou Hua’s leg and does not look at the window. For a while.
chapters.epigraph: “You remind me of someone. A physician’s assistant we had, three years ago.” — Commander Zhou Hua, from the bed

chapters.title: Morning Rounds and a Moved Chair
chapters.desc: Someone has moved a chair to where she sits. She knows who.
chapters.epigraph: “You read the camp records.” “Several kinds of records pointing to the same pattern.”

chapters.title: Chen Ye’s One True Thing
chapters.desc: On the way out of the inn, Chen Ye tells her what she has been afraid to guess.
chapters.epigraph: “I have served him for nine years and I have never seen him move a chair.” — Chen Ye

chapters.title: The Fifth Day
chapters.desc: The officer is fit to travel, and the General asks for all of her records.
chapters.epigraph: “Not only the summary. All of them.” — the General, on her three years of records

chapters.title: What Arrives Three Days Later
chapters.desc: A letter from her uncle, and one paragraph at the end that changes everything.
chapters.epigraph: “If it doesn’t become anything else, I will still have known something real.” “Of course.” — Mei Yun, not looking up

chapters.title: The Letter He Writes Himself
chapters.desc: For the first time, the handwriting on the letter is his.
chapters.epigraph: The records format is at your discretion. You know them better than the commission’s rules do. — a letter, in his own hand

chapters.title: Two Weeks
chapters.desc: The letters come every two weeks. Her mother has noticed.
chapters.epigraph: “I have watched you for nineteen years. I am not going to ask you anything.” — Lady Ren

chapters.title: What the Emperor Hears
chapters.desc: The Emperor asks one question about the physician, and his nephew forgets to stop talking.
chapters.epigraph: “Tell me about the consulting physician.” — the Emperor, who already knew the answer would take a while

chapters.title: Three Months
chapters.desc: Three months until the capital, and he keeps doing small, exact things for her family.
chapters.epigraph: I read your father’s regional herb survey eleven years ago. It was rigorous. — the General, unrevised

chapters.title: The Capital
chapters.desc: A green coat, a jade hairpin, and the first dinner in the same room.
chapters.epigraph: “He looked back at you before he crossed the courtyard. After Lin Wenyuan called his name. He looked back.”

chapters.title: The Presentation
chapters.desc: She stands before the court with three years of work. He watches.
chapters.epigraph: “You looked very well in the green coat.” “I am simply observing.”

chapters.title: The Dinner and What Follows
chapters.desc: In a lantern-lit courtyard, he says he will come to Qingzhou. Not only for the review.
chapters.epigraph: “I know your language. I have been learning it for a long time.” — in a lantern-lit courtyard, the capital

chapters.title: The Morning of Departure
chapters.desc: She asks him what the other reasons are. He answers in one word.
chapters.epigraph: “You said and for other reasons. What are the other reasons?”

chapters.title: The Road Home
chapters.desc: Three months to wait, and this time she doesn’t mind.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t need to confirm. I was there.” “I know you were there. I want to hear you say it.” — Mei Yun, on the road home

chapters.title: Three Months Later
chapters.desc: The clinic door opens, and the General is standing in her front room.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to find the words for it. I know.”

chapters.title: The Dinner Her Mother Had Planned for Months
chapters.desc: He comes to dinner with a gift for her father, and her mother asks if he eats alone.
chapters.epigraph: “You have no family in the capital? No household to return to in the evenings?” — Lady Ren, who had planned this for months
chapters.volume: Volume Seven: The Dinner and the Storm

chapters.title: Peng Yao
chapters.desc: A pleasant new secretary delivers papers in person and looks at the wrong cabinet.
chapters.epigraph: “He looked at your bookshelves. For longer than the left.” — Mei Yun, on the new secretary
chapters.volume: Volume Seven: The Dinner and the Storm

chapters.title: The Third Day
chapters.desc: The last day of the review, and he tells her what he sees in her work.
chapters.epigraph: “You have never once overestimated a clinical outcome in three years of records.” — the General, on the third day
chapters.volume: Volume Seven: The Dinner and the Storm

chapters.title: Peng Yao, Again
chapters.desc: Peng Yao keeps asking about the letters, and she asks the General not to manage around her.
chapters.epigraph: Yes. You are right. I will not manage around you again. — eleven words, morning light, the clinic window
chapters.volume: Volume Seven: The Dinner and the Storm

chapters.title: The Storm
chapters.desc: A notice arrives to stop the letters. She writes to ask if he allowed it.
chapters.epigraph: “The complication is administrative.” “Administrative.” — Lady Ren, who had been reading situations her whole life
chapters.volume: Volume Seven: The Dinner and the Storm

chapters.title: What Peng Yao Does
chapters.desc: A formal complaint names them both, and Peng Yao comes to the clinic to watch her hear about it.
chapters.epigraph: “I wanted to inform you.” “Thank you for telling me. I will make a note of this visit in the clinic records.”

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.desc: Four pages in his hand, and a promise to say it plainly to anyone who asks.
chapters.epigraph: There are things I want to say that have been waiting for the right time. — four pages, written without sleep

chapters.title: The Riverbank
chapters.desc: A child falls at the second bend. She goes alone. Peng Yao is waiting.
chapters.epigraph: “Move aside, please.” — Yun Shiyu, at the second bend, with her bag

chapters.title: What the General Knows
chapters.desc: The report reaches him on the road: no body recovered.
chapters.epigraph: “We are not stopping for the night. We move now.” — the General, on the northern road

chapters.title: Dead or Alive
chapters.desc: He finds her hairpin below the gorge, and rides to the Emperor for permission to cross the border.
chapters.epigraph: “Bring her back, Lingyun.” — the Emperor

chapters.title: The Letter at the Border Post
chapters.desc: At the flooded border, a letter in charcoal and a pouch embroidered with clouds.
chapters.epigraph: “She says not to let anyone cross for her.” “I would point out that you are anyone.” — Chen Ye, at the border post

chapters.title: The River Doctor
chapters.desc: Thirteen days on the far side of the river, and one question she can’t stop asking: who was behind her?
chapters.epigraph: “Look where you’re going, little goose.” — Old Nai, Wide Water

chapters.title: A Lamp for the Midwife

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
In another life, Yun Shiyu was a trauma surgeon. In this one she is sixteen, the governor’s daughter in a rainy southern river city, and she has just watched the Emperor’s nephew ride past her balcony.

She does something very foolish to see him again. It turns into six weeks in an army medical tent, three years building a clinic of her own, and a slow, careful love carried mostly in letters — until someone decides to use those letters against them both.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
This is a slow, gentle romance, but some chapters include:

• Battle wounds and field surgery, described from a physician’s point of view

• A near-drowning and an attempted murder (The Riverbank)

• A dislocated shoulder put back in, and a fever (The River Doctor)

• A difficult childbirth, not graphic (A Lamp for the Midwife)

• Grief and fear while a loved one is missing

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
I started this one because I wanted a romance where two people fall in love by watching each other be good at their work. She stitches his arm. He reads her reports at night. Nobody says anything for a very long time, and somehow everybody around them notices anyway.

He isn’t cold. He’s careful. She isn’t quiet. She’s honest. That’s most of the story, really.

It ran longer than I planned. I kept thinking they were nearly there and then one of them would write another letter. Thank you for waiting with them all the way to the end.

A small note: names are written without tone marks in the chapters so they’re easier to read. If you want to know how to say them, the Characters and Names & Terms pages have the Chinese.

— 甜慕

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Qingzhou — Shiyu’s home city in the rainy south, known for herbs and river trade. Her father is its governor.
The capital — Where the Emperor and the court live, about four days north of Qingzhou by carriage.
The northern camp — The Northern Army’s base on the frontier, three days from Qingzhou. Uncle Xiang runs its medical tent.
Qingcloud Medical Hall (清云医馆) — The clinic Shiyu opens at seventeen.
The Fairy Physician — What Qingzhou calls Shiyu. She thinks it is excessive.
The Five — Zhan Lingyun’s most trusted officers: Wei Tiecheng, Lin Wenyuan, Zhou Hua, Lü Yue and Chen Ye.
The Civilian Medical Commission — The army’s new office for bringing civilian physicians and records into its medical work. Shiyu becomes its chief civilian physician.
The hour of the Rabbit — The old name for the two hours around dawn, roughly five to seven in the morning.
Li — A distance of about half a kilometre. Five hundred li is a long journey.
Relay station — Post stations along the main roads where riders change horses, so urgent letters can travel hundreds of li in a day.
The Censorate — The court office that investigates complaints against officials.
The Ministry of Revenue / Ministry of Justice — Two of the great government ministries in the capital.
The second bend — A fast stretch of river in Qingzhou’s western district, just above the gorge.
Wide Water — A fishing village across the border, where the river spreads out and slows down.
The cloud-embroidered pouch — A small silk pouch Shiyu’s mother made for her. She presses it when there is something she can’t say.
Saying the names — Shiyu: “shir-yoo”. Lingyun: “ling-yoon”. Zhan: “jahn”. Xiang: “shyahng”. Lü Yue: “lyoo yweh”. Qingzhou: “ching-joe”.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
In high school, Tang Xi was the girl everyone knew, and Wang An Yu was the boy who only talked about exams. She followed him into the library anyway.

Years later he chairs An-Tech Holdings, and she’s the account manager from the outside agency that runs his marketing, so quiet now that she won’t meet his eyes. He asked for her by name. She doesn’t work for him, and that matters.

Then he says her old nickname across a conference table, and they both remember exactly who they used to be.

Second chance · A high-school crush, grown up · Office romance without a boss · Coming soon

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
I didn’t want a boss chasing his employee. So she works for the agency, not for him, and the turning point is her taking herself off his account so they can meet as equals.

It’s charged and held back: years of looks finally spent, an office after hours, a tie loosened, glasses off. He’s in control until she uses the nickname. Then he isn’t.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Ren Hao fixes problems for big companies: kidnappings, scandals, the things that never make the news. He’s loud, direct and used to being obeyed. Xu Song-Zhu rebuilds what happened from the wreckage: flight recorders, ruined hard drives, the last minutes of strangers.

His sister sets them up at a French restaurant with candles. He orders her water and suggests she wash her face. She laughs, leans across the table and tells him he’s awfully bossy for a man who hasn’t asked her name.

Then a plane goes into the sea, and the woman he loves is the one who has to listen to how it ended.

Opposites · Loud hero · She makes him say it · Coming soon

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
This one is loud and quick and joyful, and then, when it has to be, very quiet. Her job means listening to people’s last words, and the book doesn’t look away from what that costs her.

He tries to love her the way he protects clients, with fireproofing and assistants and flowers. She wants the words. Watching a man like that learn to say them is the whole fun of it.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Yen Si-Yuan is the most famous of the Yen triplets, an actress on billboards across Asia. Yang Pengcheng is the lawyer sent to clean up a legal mess on her film set, and the only man in the room who isn’t starstruck. She decides he’s a challenge. He decides she’s a logical match.

For three years she bows at his family’s dinners while they ignore her, and he says nothing. When his mother humiliates her at a gala in front of everyone, he says nothing again.

She moves her filming overseas and puts an ocean between them. For the first time in his life, Yang Pengcheng finds out what silence costs.

A marriage in trouble · He has to earn her back · Second chance · Coming soon

authorNote.title: Author Note

This is the book in the series that hurts on purpose: a marriage gone cold, and a man who has to learn that staying silent is a choice, and never a neutral one.

The repair is slow and earned. You’ll see it in how he touches her. He falls asleep on her shoulder during script reads.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Yen Si-Jie sat in the front row of a criminal-psychology seminar with hearts in her eyes while everyone else was frightened of the guest lecturer. Arthur Cheung profiles the city’s worst people for a living. He agreed to date her because she was the only person he’d ever met who didn’t hide her motives.

She sends twenty texts in a row. She sits on his lap while he reads case files. Then she finds his notebook, full of her moods and reactions in neat columns.

Is she his girlfriend or his experiment? And why is his newest case circling closer to her?

Sunshine and the cold one · Clingy heroine · A profiler in love · Coming soon

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Arthur’s notebook isn’t creepy. It’s his clumsy way of learning how to love someone, because nobody ever taught him. ‘I’m not studying you. I’m learning you.’

It’s playful and intense, with a thriller running under a sweet romance. The man who reads everyone can’t read her in bed, and she makes him say what he wants.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Yen Si-Wei, the youngest triplet, is the coldest girl in business school, and she likes it that way. Nobody looks closely at a mean girl, so nobody notices her quietly funding scholarships and ending bullies’ careers.

Geum Sung Jae runs the Iron Dogs, the crew that polices the city’s grey market, and he only goes after predators. He sees through her mask on the first day. She sees through his on the second.

After every fight she cleans his wounds and lectures him, and somewhere between the antiseptic and the bandages they start kissing. Then the Deng family’s men move into his district, and he starts to fear she’ll choose a clean boy from her own world.

Enemies to lovers · Secret softies · She patches him up · Coming soon

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Rough and tender. The fights are physical and they hurt, and the tenderness is all in the cleaning up afterwards. His big hands are careful with her.

Sung Jae fell first and fell hard. His flaw is believing he isn’t good enough for her, and her job in this book is to make him stop pretending to be a monster just because he’s good at it.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
He Xiao-Rong is the golden girl of her university’s dance programme and a rising creator online. After a terrible break-up she hides at her local market in a tattered hoodie, grabbing comfort oranges from the fruit stall where she keeps a monthly tab.

Lu Han-Wei, a former esports pro who now runs a tiny game studio, is covering his family’s stall that morning. He grabs her arm and calls her a thief in front of the whole market.

She pulls down her hood. He realises he has just terrified the dancer whose videos he has studied for a year as the model for every movement in his game. He starts turning up at her rehearsals with iced tea and a bag of oranges to say sorry, and doesn’t stop.

Awkward meeting · Gamer hero · Dancer heroine · Coming soon

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
The lightest book on the list: warm, funny and a bit nerdy. Late-night streams, pizza boxes, headsets off, and two people who narrate their dates like a game until they forget to.

They both have real work pressure, crunch for him and injuries and auditions for her, and the book takes their jobs seriously.

novels.ideaNote: Planned: 50 chapters. The Archive · The Noise · The Files · Matched · Side stories.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Deng Mu-Ran, the theatrical second son of an old dynasty, breaks into the Iron Archive to wipe the files his family keeps on him. He doesn’t expect the night-shift engineer, He Si-Mei, to drop out of the air vents and very nearly win. He also doesn’t expect to find out that his family pays her wages.

Months later he corners her in an abandoned industrial park to test her, and she picks up a steel pipe. Now he wants a rematch every Sunday. He wants to buy her lab, guard her building and clear her path.

She wants him to understand that she doesn’t want to be kept. She wants to be matched.

Rivals to lovers · Sparring partners · Two geniuses · Coming soon

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Two geniuses who only feel awake when they’re fighting each other, and a man whose flaw is trying to buy and guard someone’s life instead of asking her what she wants.

There are no forced kisses or threats in this one. The love scenes start like a fight and end in surrender on both sides. He only sleeps with his head in her lap.

descs.en: She saved him with her savings. He married her and made her world smaller. The day she books the flight to Vienna herself, their love story starts.

novels.ideaNote: Planned: 50 chapters. The Alley · The Cage · Vienna · Without a Lock · Side stories.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Su Yue-Sheng, a world-class cellist from a fallen family, found a bleeding stranger in an alley and nursed him back to health with everything she had. Deng Kai let her. He was never as fragile as she thought; the attack was his own test of his enemies. He married the woman who saved him, and then, lovingly and carefully, began to keep the world out.

Her hands are insured for millions, so she mustn’t cook. Vienna is cold, so she mustn’t tour.

The night he cancels her tour for her health, she puts down her bow and books the flight herself. He can come as her husband, she tells him, or stay as her warden.

Dark romance · A controlling hero who has to change · Musician heroine · Coming soon

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
This will be the heaviest book in the series, and I want to write it honestly. Deng Kai’s love is real, and it has a lock on it. The book won’t romanticise that. He has to change for real, and it takes a long time.

The love scenes come late, after he has changed, on her terms: she leads, he asks, and the door stays open.
